questions.question: What is the primary function of a Load Balancer in the context of AWS cloud infrastructure?

options.text: It stores backups of EC2 instances across Availability Zones
It controls security groups to restrict network access
It distributes incoming traffic across multiple targets in different Availability Zones
It provisions new EC2 instances when traffic increases

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. It distributes incoming traffic across multiple targets in different Availability Zones
questions.explanation: Load balancers in AWS (e.g., Elastic Load Balancing - ELB) are designed to automatically distribute incoming application or network traffic across multiple targets, such as EC2 instances, containers (ECS), Lambda functions, or even IP addresses. They improve fault tolerance and ensure high availability by routing traffic to healthy targets in different Availability Zones.

incorrectExplanations.A:
It stores backups of EC2 instances across Availability Zones
This is the role of services like Amazon S3 or AWS Backup, not load balancers.
incorrectExplanations.B:
It controls security groups to restrict network access
Security groups and network ACLs handle access control, not traffic distribution.
incorrectExplanations.D:
It provisions new EC2 instances when traffic increases
This is handled by Auto Scaling, not by the load balancer itself.

questions.question: In the context of an AWS Elastic Load Balancer, what is the role of a listener, and why is defining a default rule important?

options.text: A listener encrypts data in transit and requires a default rule to apply rate limiting to the target group
A listener monitors backend instance health and routes traffic using availability metrics
A listener checks for incoming client connections and uses the default rule when no other conditions are met
A listener logs incoming requests and automatically assigns priorities to all target groups

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. A listener checks for incoming client connections and uses the default rule when no other conditions are met
questions.explanation:
In AWS, a listener is a process that checks for incoming connection requests based on the protocol and port you define (e.g., HTTP on port 80 or HTTPS on port 443).
Each listener must have at least one default rule, which defines how to route requests if none of the custom listener rules match. This rule specifies a target group, a condition (such as a path pattern), and a priority to determine the order of rule evaluation.

incorrectExplanations.A:
A listener encrypts data in transit and requires a default rule to apply rate limiting to the target group
Listeners can use HTTPS for encrypted traffic, but they do not apply rate limits that are handled by other AWS services (e.g., AWS WAF or API Gateway).
incorrectExplanations.B:
A listener monitors backend instance health and routes traffic using availability metrics
Health checks are performed by the load balancer itself, not the listener.
incorrectExplanations.D:
A listener logs incoming requests and automatically assigns priorities to all target groups
Listeners do not assign priorities automatically; you manually define rule priorities. Logging is done through Access Logs, a separate feature.

technicalReview.reason: The source describes conditions and priority as part of the ALB default rule. AWS handles these separately.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the primary benefit of using AWS Direct Connect over a standard internet connection?

options.text: It provides automatic encryption and data loss prevention between VPCs
It allows private, dedicated network connectivity between your on-premises network and AWS, bypassing the public internet
It automatically replicates EC2 instances across Availability Zones without user configuration
It enables serverless applications to be hosted entirely outside the AWS Cloud

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. It allows private, dedicated network connectivity between your on-premises network and AWS, bypassing the public internet

incorrectExplanations.A:
It provides automatic encryption and data loss prevention between VPCs
Direct Connect does not encrypt traffic by default; you must implement encryption separately (e.g., IPsec VPN over Direct Connect).
incorrectExplanations.C:
It automatically replicates EC2 instances across Availability Zones without user configuration
EC2 replication across AZs must be configured by the user using services like Auto Scaling or Load Balancers.
incorrectExplanations.D:
It enables serverless applications to be hosted entirely outside the AWS Cloud
Serverless apps (e.g., using AWS Lambda) still run within AWS; Direct Connect doesn’t enable external hosting.

questions.question: You are designing a highly available network architecture using AWS Direct Connect. Which configuration ensures automatic failover while maintaining active traffic flow through both connections?

options.text: Virtual Private Gateway with Route 53 failover
Public Virtual Interface over a single connection

questions.explanation: The Active/Active (BGP multipath) setup in AWS Direct Connect enables both connections to be active simultaneously, facilitating load balancing of traffic and automatically rerouting it if one path fails. It's the default configuration for high availability using Border Gateway Protocol (BGP).

incorrectExplanations.A:
Active/Passive with BGP
Only one connection is active; the other is used only during failover, not ideal for active load sharing.
incorrectExplanations.B:
Virtual Private Gateway with Route 53 failover
Route 53 handles DNS-based failover, not Direct Connect link-level redundancy.
incorrectExplanations.D:
Public Virtual Interface over a single connection
This setup lacks redundancy; a single link means no failover capability.

questions.question: What is the CloudFormation Designer primarily used for?

options.text: Monitoring EC2 instance performance in real time
Creating, viewing, and modifying CloudFormation templates using a graphical interface
Managing IAM policies across multiple AWS accounts
Performing backup and recovery of S3 buckets

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. Creating, viewing, and modifying CloudFormation templates using a graphical interface
questions.explanation: CloudFormation Designer is a visual tool provided by AWS that lets users design infrastructure templates using a drag-and-drop interface. It also includes built-in JSON/YAML editors for direct editing of the templates.

incorrectExplanations.A:
Monitoring EC2 instance performance in real time
That is done using Amazon CloudWatch, not CloudFormation Designer.
incorrectExplanations.C:
Managing IAM policies across multiple AWS accounts
IAM policies are managed through IAM, and cross-account access involves AWS Organizations or STS, not CloudFormation Designer.
incorrectExplanations.D:
Performing backup and recovery of S3 buckets
AWS Backup or lifecycle policies manage S3 backups—not CloudFormation Designer.

technicalReview.reason: Review legacy graphical tooling terminology against AWS Infrastructure Composer.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding Amazon CloudWatch Metrics?

options.text: CloudWatch metrics can be deleted manually to reduce storage costs
Memory and disk usage metrics for EC2 instances are available by default
Metric timestamps can be backdated up to one month if needed
CloudWatch metrics automatically expire after 15 months if no new data is published

questions.sourceAnswerKey: D. CloudWatch metrics automatically expire after 15 months if no new data is published
questions.explanation: CloudWatch metrics expire after 15 months if no new data points are published. This retention policy helps manage storage automatically. As new data arrives, older data beyond 15 months is dropped. You cannot manually delete a metric.

incorrectExplanations.A:
CloudWatch metrics can be deleted manually to reduce storage costs
Metrics cannot be manually deleted; they expire based on age and data updates.
incorrectExplanations.B:
Memory and disk usage metrics for EC2 instances are available by default
These require the CloudWatch Agent to be installed on the EC2 instance.
incorrectExplanations.C:
Metric timestamps can be backdated up to one month if needed
CloudWatch only accepts timestamps up to 2 weeks in the past.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key benefit of using Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive for data storage?

options.text: It allows instant data retrieval with millisecond latency
It is designed for frequently accessed data across multiple regions
It provides the lowest-cost storage option for long-term data retention with retrieval times up to 48 hours
It automatically replicates data to on-premises tape libraries for backup

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. It provides the lowest-cost storage option for long-term data retention with retrieval times up to 48 hours
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive is ideal for rarely accessed data, such as backups and archives. It offers very low storage costs, and while retrieval is not instant, bulk retrieval can return large amounts of data within up to 48 hours, and standard restores are available within 12 hours or less. Data is stored across at least 3 Availability Zones with 11 nines (99.999999999%) durability.

incorrectExplanations.A:
It allows instant data retrieval with millisecond latency
That’s true for S3 Standard or S3 Intelligent-Tiering, not Glacier Deep Archive.
incorrectExplanations.B:
It is designed for frequently accessed data across multiple regions
Glacier Deep Archive is meant for infrequent access, not frequent or real-time access.
incorrectExplanations.D:
It automatically replicates data to on-premises tape libraries for backup
AWS does not replicate to on-premises systems; it stores data within the AWS Cloud infrastructure.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes how Amazon S3 Object Lock protects objects?

options.text: It encrypts objects during upload and automatically deletes them after 30 days
It prevents objects from being deleted or overwritten for a specified time or until a legal hold is removed
It moves objects to Glacier storage for long-term protection
It compresses objects to save space and locks the entire S3 bucket permanently

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. It prevents objects from being deleted or overwritten for a specified time or until a legal hold is removed
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Object Lock enables you to lock individual object versions to prevent deletion or modification. You can enforce this via a retention period (fixed time) or a legal hold (remains until explicitly removed). It is useful for regulatory compliance and data immutability. Object Lock only works with versioned buckets.

incorrectExplanations.A:
It encrypts objects during upload and automatically deletes them after 30 days
Encryption and lifecycle policies are separate features; Object Lock prevents deletion, not triggers it.
incorrectExplanations.C:
It moves objects to Glacier storage for long-term protection
Object Lock is not a storage class; it works with objects regardless of their storage class.
incorrectExplanations.D:
It compresses objects to save space and locks the entire S3 bucket permanently
Locking is done per object version, not for the entire bucket; and it does not compress objects.

questions.question: Which of the following is the recommended method for interacting with Amazon S3, considering current API support?

options.text: Using the SOAP API over HTTP for full feature compatibility
Using the REST API with virtual hosting and HTTP requests
Using FTP for faster object transfers
Using only the AWS CLI as the exclusive method for S3 access

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. Using the REST API with virtual hosting and HTTP requests
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 supports multiple access methods, but SOAP support over HTTP is deprecated, and new features are not added to the SOAP API. The REST API is the recommended method for interacting with S3 and can be used with virtual hosting via the HTTP Host header. Alternatively, AWS SDKs (built on REST) offer a more user-friendly interface.

incorrectExplanations.A:
Using the SOAP API over HTTP for full feature compatibility
SOAP over HTTP is deprecated, and new S3 features are not supported on SOAP.
incorrectExplanations.C:
Using FTP for faster object transfers
Amazon S3 does not support FTP; transfers are done via HTTP-based APIs or tools like AWS CLI.
incorrectExplanations.D:
Using only the AWS CLI as the exclusive method for S3 access
While the AWS CLI is useful, it is not the only method—REST API and SDKs are also commonly used.

questions.question: How can you use CloudWatch Log Streams to better understand the execution of your AWS Lambda function?

options.text: By enabling encryption at rest for Lambda artifacts
By writing custom logging statements in your Lambda code to track execution flow
By enabling automatic backups of function logs every 24 hours
By configuring S3 triggers to create CloudWatch dashboards

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. By writing custom logging statements in your Lambda code to track execution flow
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda automatically sends invocation logs to CloudWatch Logs. Developers can add custom logging statements (e.g., console.log() in Node.js or print() in Python) within the Lambda code. These logs appear in CloudWatch Log Streams, helping you trace the execution flow, debug errors, and measure performance.

incorrectExplanations.A:
By enabling encryption at rest for Lambda artifacts
Encryption at rest secures data but doesn't help analyze execution flow.
incorrectExplanations.C:
By enabling automatic backups of function logs every 24 hours
CloudWatch Logs retains data, but there is no built-in automatic backup for logs in this way.
incorrectExplanations.D:
By configuring S3 triggers to create CloudWatch dashboards
S3 triggers invoke Lambda functions, but they don’t generate dashboards directly.

questions.question: In an Amazon Aurora DB cluster, what is the primary role of the Aurora Replica?

options.text: It performs both read and write operations on a separate storage volume
It mirrors the primary instance to provide instant backups only
It supports read-only operations and can be promoted during failover
It replicates data from the primary instance using snapshot-based syncing

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. It supports read-only operations and can be promoted during failover
questions.explanation: Aurora Replicas are read-only instances that connect to the same shared storage as the primary. They help offload read traffic and are also candidates for automated failover if the primary instance becomes unavailable. You can configure failover priority for each replica.

incorrectExplanations.A: Aurora Replicas do not perform write operations and do not use separate storage volumes.
incorrectExplanations.B: They do not act only as backup mirrors; they handle real-time read workloads.
incorrectExplanations.D: Aurora uses shared storage, not snapshot-based replication for read replicas.

questions.question: What happens in an Aurora DB cluster when the primary DB instance fails?

options.text: The database becomes read-only until a new cluster is manually provisioned
An Aurora Replica is automatically promoted to the new primary DB instance
Data is lost unless a recent snapshot is restored
A secondary storage volume is mounted as a temporary write target

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. An Aurora Replica is automatically promoted to the new primary DB instance
questions.explanation: Aurora offers automatic failover. If the primary instance fails, Aurora promotes a replica (based on priority settings) to act as the new primary, maintaining high availability without manual intervention.

incorrectExplanations.A: Aurora ensures high availability by automatic failover—it doesn’t go read-only indefinitely.
incorrectExplanations.C: Aurora provides durable shared storage, so no data is lost on instance of failure.
incorrectExplanations.D: Aurora does not use secondary volumes; it relies on shared cluster storage.

questions.question: Which components are required to establish a VPN connection between your on-premises data center and an Amazon VPC?

options.text: A NAT gateway and a Route 53 hosted zone
An internet gateway and an EC2 instance with a public IP
A virtual private gateway in AWS and a customer gateway in your data center
A load balancer and a CloudFront distribution

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. A virtual private gateway in AWS and a customer gateway in your data centre
questions.explanation:
To set up a site-to-site VPN with AWS, you need two components:
A Virtual Private Gateway (VGW) on the AWS side, attached to your VPC
A Customer Gateway (CGW) on your end, typically a physical or software-based VPN device in your data centre
These work together to establish a secure IPsec VPN tunnel.

incorrectExplanations.A: NAT Gateway and Route 53 are unrelated to VPN connections.
incorrectExplanations.B: An internet gateway allows public internet access but doesn’t establish a VPN tunnel.
incorrectExplanations.D: Load balancers and CloudFront are used for content delivery and traffic distribution, not for VPN connectivity.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a VPN-only subnet in an Amazon VPC?

options.text: It connects directly to the internet using an internet gateway
It does not have any route to external networks
It uses a virtual private gateway to connect to a remote network over a VPN
It is used to host public-facing applications like web servers

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. It uses a virtual private gateway to connect to a remote network over a VPN
questions.explanation: A VPN-only subnet is designed to route traffic through a virtual private gateway (VGW) instead of an internet gateway. This setup is commonly used for private, secure connectivity between your AWS VPC and your on-premises data center over a VPN connection.

incorrectExplanations.A: That describes a public subnet, which is connected to the internet via an internet gateway.
incorrectExplanations.B: VPN-only subnets do have routes, but through a VGW, not the internet.
incorrectExplanations.D: Public subnets are used for hosting public-facing apps, not VPN-only subnets.

questions.question: You are managing a VPC peering connection that is currently in the pending-acceptance state. As the owner of the requester VPC, what action must you take if you need to add a new CIDR block to your VPC?

options.text: Add the CIDR block immediately since changes are allowed at any stage
Accept the peering request first, then add the CIDR block
Delete the current peering request, add the CIDR block, and then create a new peering request
Ask the acceptor VPC owner to add a matching CIDR block first

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. Delete the current peering request, add the CIDR block, and then create a new peering request
questions.explanation: When a VPC peering connection is in the pending-acceptance state, the requester VPC owner is not allowed to add new CIDR blocks. To proceed, they must delete the current peering request, modify the CIDR block, and re-initiate a new peering request.

incorrectExplanations.A: CIDR block modifications are not allowed in the pending-acceptance state for the requester.
incorrectExplanations.B: The requester cannot accept the request—they can only initiate or delete it.
incorrectExplanations.D: The accepter adding a matching CIDR block would likely cause an overlap conflict, not solve it.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of associating a route table with a subnet in an Amazon VPC?

options.text: To define the encryption rules for data in transit
To control which EC2 instance types can be launched
To specify the routes for outbound traffic from the subnet
To set user access permissions for the subnet

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. To specify the routes for outbound traffic from the subnet
questions.explanation: Every subnet in a VPC must be associated with a route table, which defines how outbound traffic is directed, for example, whether it goes to an internet gateway, a NAT gateway, or stays within the VPC. If a custom route table is not explicitly associated, the main route table is used by default.

incorrectExplanations.A: Route tables don’t handle encryption—that’s done by security groups, TLS, or VPN.
incorrectExplanations.B: EC2 instance types are controlled by region and quotas, not route tables.
incorrectExplanations.D: User access is managed via IAM policies, not route tables.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about Security Groups in Amazon VPC?

options.text: A newly created security group allows all inbound and outbound traffic by default
You can associate only one security group with an EC2 instance
Security groups control traffic at the instance level and are associated with network interfaces
If no security group is specified, the instance will be blocked from all network communication

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. Security groups control traffic at the instance level and are associated with network interfaces
questions.explanation: Security groups in AWS act as virtual firewalls that control inbound and outbound traffic at the instance level. They are actually applied to the network interfaces attached to the instance. You can associate up to 5 security groups with an instance.

incorrectExplanations.A: A newly created security group has no inbound rules, and only one outbound rule allowing all outbound traffic.
incorrectExplanations.B: You can associate up to 5 security groups with an instance, not just one.
incorrectExplanations.D: If no security group is specified, the instance is associated with the default security group, which allows inbound traffic from other instances in the same group and outbound traffic to all destinations.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid use case for Amazon VPC Flow Logs?

options.text: Encrypting data in transit between EC2 instances
Diagnosing overly restrictive security group rules by analysing network traffic
Creating custom IAM roles for EC2 traffic analysis
Automatically patching network vulnerabilities in your VPC

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. Diagnosing overly restrictive security group rules by analysing network traffic
questions.explanation: VPC Flow Logs capture information about IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in your VPC. This data helps you monitor traffic, verify if traffic is being blocked, and determine whether security group rules or NACLs are too restrictive.

incorrectExplanations.A: Flow Logs only monitor traffic; they do not encrypt it.
incorrectExplanations.C: IAM roles are unrelated to Flow Logs; they control permissions, not traffic analysis.
incorrectExplanations.D: Flow Logs do not fix or patch vulnerabilities—they only report on traffic patterns.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about network interfaces (ENIs) in Amazon EC2 is correct?

options.text: A primary network interface can be detached and moved to another instance
Each network interface must have exactly one IPv6 address
A network interface can include multiple private IPv4 addresses and one or more security groups
Public IPv4 addresses are assigned to all secondary network interfaces by default

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. A network interface can include multiple private IPv4 addresses and one or more security groups
questions.explanation:
An Elastic Network Interface (ENI) can include:
A primary private IPv4 address
One or more secondary private IPv4 addresses
One or more security groups
Optionally, a public IPv4 address (for eth0)
IPv6 addresses, MAC address, EIP, etc.

incorrectExplanations.A: The primary ENI (eth0) cannot be detached from an instance.
incorrectExplanations.B: IPv6 addresses are optional, and you can have more than one—or none.
incorrectExplanations.D: Public IPv4 addresses are only auto-assigned to the primary interface (eth0), not to secondary ENIs by default.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about route tables in an Amazon VPC?

options.text: A subnet can be associated with multiple route tables simultaneously
You can delete the main route table if it's no longer in use
Route tables use the most specific matching rule to determine the traffic path
Route tables automatically update to include new gateways or connections

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. Route tables use the most specific matching rule to determine the traffic path
questions.explanation: Route tables apply the longest prefix match rule, meaning they select the most specific route that matches the destination IP address. This ensures accurate and optimized routing decisions.

incorrectExplanations.A: A subnet can be associated with only one route table at a time.
incorrectExplanations.B: The main route table cannot be deleted, though it can be replaced with a custom one.
incorrectExplanations.D: You must manually update route tables to add routes for new gateways or connections.

questions.question: Which of the following is required to allow an EC2 instance in a public subnet to access the internet via IPv4?

options.text: Assign an IAM role to the instance
Enable CloudTrail logs on the subnet
Attach an Internet Gateway to the VPC and update the route table

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. Attach an Internet Gateway to the VPC and update the route table
questions.explanation:
To enable internet access for an EC2 instance via IPv4, you must:
Attach an Internet Gateway (IGW) to your VPC
Ensure the route table for the subnet has a route to the IGW
Assign a public IP or Elastic IP to the instance
Configure security groups and NACLs to allow relevant traffic

incorrectExplanations.A: IAM roles control permissions to AWS services, not internet connectivity.
incorrectExplanations.B: CloudTrail logs are for auditing, not for managing internet access.
incorrectExplanations.D: Auto Scaling helps manage instance count, but does not provide internet access.

questions.question: What is the primary function of an Egress-Only Internet Gateway in an Amazon VPC?

options.text: To allow both inbound and outbound IPv6 traffic between the Internet and your VPC
To provide outbound-only IPv6 access from your VPC to the internet, blocking inbound connections
To route IPv4 traffic through a NAT instance for private subnets
To enable DNS resolution for instances in the VPC

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. To provide outbound-only IPv6 access from your VPC to the internet, blocking inbound connections
questions.explanation: An Egress-Only Internet Gateway (EOIGW) enables outbound-only IPv6 traffic from instances in your VPC to the internet. It prevents the internet from initiating IPv6 connections to your instances, thereby enhancing security for IPv6-enabled environments.

incorrectExplanations.A: Egress Only Internet Gateways do not allow inbound traffic—only outbound is permitted.
incorrectExplanations.C: That describes a NAT gateway/instance, which is for IPv4, not IPv6.
incorrectExplanations.D: DNS resolution is managed by AmazonProvidedDNS or Route 53, not an Egress Only Internet Gateway.

questions.question: Which of the following statements accurately describes the behavior and configuration requirements of a NAT Gateway in AWS?

options.text: It allows inbound connections from the internet to instances in a private subnet
It must be deployed in a private subnet and requires a public IP to function
It enables instances in private subnets to initiate internet-bound traffic using a public subnet’s Elastic IP
It supports VPC peering and VPN traffic routing by default

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. It enables instances in private subnets to initiate internet-bound traffic using a public subnet’s Elastic IP
questions.explanation: A NAT Gateway is placed in a public subnet, where it uses an Elastic IP to allow outbound-only internet access for instances in private subnets. It blocks inbound connections, supports TCP, UDP, and ICMP, and is commonly used to access AWS services or download software updates.

incorrectExplanations.A: NAT Gateways do not allow inbound connections from the Internet.
incorrectExplanations.B: A NAT Gateway must be deployed in a public subnet, not a private one.
incorrectExplanations.D: NAT Gateways cannot route traffic over VPC endpoints, VPNs, Direct Connect, or peering connections.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about Elastic IP addresses (EIPs) in AWS?

options.text: They are automatically released when the associated instance is stopped
You are charged extra only when the EIP is actively used by a running instance
EIPs are static public IPv4 addresses that remain allocated to your account until you release them
You can associate an Elastic IP with multiple instances at the same time

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. EIPs are static public IPv4 addresses that remain allocated to your account until you release them
questions.explanation: Elastic IPs (EIPs) are static public IPv4 addresses provided by AWS. They remain associated with your account until you explicitly release them, regardless of whether they're in use or not. AWS charges you when an EIP is not associated with a running instance or is attached to a stopped instance.

incorrectExplanations.A: EIPs are not automatically released when the instance stops—you must release them manually.
incorrectExplanations.B: Charges apply when the EIP is not associated with a running instance—not when actively used.
incorrectExplanations.D: An EIP can be associated with only one instance or network interface at a time.

questions.question: In AWS Systems Manager Automation, what is a step?

options.text: A backup of the Automation document stored in S3
A user permission policy applied to Automation executions
A single initiated action performed during an Automation execution, usually per target
A log file is automatically generated after the Automation completion

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. A single initiated action performed during an Automation execution, usually per target
questions.explanation: A step in Systems Manager Automation represents a discrete action executed as part of an Automation document (runbook). You can choose to run all steps simultaneously or execute them step-by-step, and each step typically targets a specific managed instance or resource.

incorrectExplanations.A: A step is not a backup; it's an execution unit in the automation workflow.
incorrectExplanations.B: IAM policies handle permissions, not step definitions.
incorrectExplanations.D: Steps generate logs, but are not logs themselves.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of using Resource Groups in AWS Systems Manager?

options.text: To group IAM users based on roles and policies
To manage and monitor a collection of resources in the same AWS Region that match defined criteria
To create backup copies of resources across multiple AWS Regions
To enforce security rules at the subnet level in a VPC

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. To manage and monitor a collection of resources in the same AWS Region that match defined criteria
questions.explanation: Resource Groups allow you to organize AWS resources (like EC2, S3, Lambda, etc.) that share common tags or attributes within the same region. You can then apply Systems Manager tools like Automation, Compliance, and Monitoring on the group as a unit.

incorrectExplanations.A: IAM groups manage users, not AWS infrastructure resources.
incorrectExplanations.C: Resource Groups don’t manage backups or cross-region replication.
incorrectExplanations.D: Subnet-level security is handled using Security Groups and Network ACLs, not Resource Groups.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about AWS access keys used for programmatic access?

options.text: An access key can be used to log in to the AWS Management Console
If the secret access key is lost, it can be retrieved from the IAM dashboard
Access keys consist of an access key ID and a secret access key used for API requests
Access keys can be shared with team members to simplify access management

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. Access keys consist of an access key ID and a secret access key used for API requests
questions.explanation:
Access keys are used for programmatic access to AWS services via the CLI, SDKs, or API. Each access key includes two parts:
Access Key ID (visible)
Secret Access Key (only shown once at creation)
If the secret key is lost, it cannot be retrieved—you must regenerate a new pair.

incorrectExplanations.A: Console logins use username and password, not access keys.
incorrectExplanations.B: You cannot retrieve a lost secret key—only regenerate it.
incorrectExplanations.D: Access keys are user-specific credentials and must not be shared.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key feature of Amazon Athena?

options.text: It requires provisioning EC2 instances to run queries
It is serverless and includes a built-in SQL query editor
It only supports querying data stored in DynamoDB
It is used for managing IAM roles and permissions

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. It is serverless and includes a built-in SQL query editor
questions.explanation: Amazon Athena is a serverless interactive query service that lets you analyze data in Amazon S3 using standard SQL. It includes a web-based query editor, so you can run queries directly from the AWS Management Console without setting up infrastructure.

incorrectExplanations.A: Athena is serverless—you do not need to provision or manage servers.
incorrectExplanations.C: Athena supports S3-based datasets, not just DynamoDB.
incorrectExplanations.D: IAM role and permission management is handled via AWS IAM, not Athena.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of AWS Budgets?

options.text: To manage VPC routing and subnet allocations
To create IAM roles and assign user permissions
To monitor and control AWS usage and costs by setting spending limits
To schedule automatic backups of EC2 instances

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. To monitor and control AWS usage and costs by setting spending limits
questions.explanation: AWS Budgets allows you to track your AWS usage, cost, and reserved instance utilization by setting custom budget thresholds. You can receive notifications when your spending approaches or exceeds the defined limits.

incorrectExplanations.A: VPC routing is handled in the VPC console, not through Budgets.
incorrectExplanations.B: IAM is used to manage roles and permissions, not costs.
incorrectExplanations.D: EC2 backups are managed via AWS Backup or custom scripts, not AWS Budgets.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of AWS Billing Conductor?

options.text: To encrypt billing data using customer-managed keys
To create IAM roles for managing budget thresholds
To group accounts for a consolidated view of cost and usage
To automatically delete unused resources to save costs

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. To group accounts for a consolidated view of cost and usage
questions.explanation: AWS Billing Conductor allows you to assign linked accounts to billing groups, providing a customized and aggregated view of cost and usage across your workloads. This is especially helpful for large organizations managing multiple accounts.

incorrectExplanations.A: Encryption of billing data is handled by AWS services, but that’s not Billing Conductor's core function.
incorrectExplanations.B: IAM roles are managed through IAM, not via Billing Conductor.
incorrectExplanations.D: Billing Conductor does not delete resources—it tracks and groups cost data.

questions.question: Which of the following is true when using AWS Billing Conductor?

options.text: Each linked account can belong to multiple billing groups simultaneously
Billing Conductor provides an aggregated view of monthly cost data for assigned account groups
Billing Conductor automatically applies service quotas based on billing group usage
You must enable Billing Conductor for each AWS Region separately

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. Billing Conductor provides an aggregated view of monthly cost data for assigned account groups
questions.explanation: Billing Conductor gives aggregated, customizable billing views for accounts assigned to a billing group. This helps organizations track costs more effectively by internal departments or projects.

incorrectExplanations.A: An account can belong to only one billing group at a time.
incorrectExplanations.C: Billing Conductor does not manage quotas; it’s focused on billing and cost tracking.
incorrectExplanations.D: Billing Conductor is a global service, not regional.

questions.question: When configuring a cost and usage report in AWS, what does selecting a time granularity of "Daily" mean?

options.text: The report will display total usage only for weekends
The report will break down cost and usage data by each individual day
The report will update every minute with real-time usage
The report will only include daily charges from EC2 instances

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. The report will break down cost and usage data by each individual day
questions.explanation: Time granularity determines how the data in your cost and usage report is aggregated. Choosing "Daily" means you will receive cost and usage data broken down by day, helping you analyze daily trends and spending patterns.

incorrectExplanations.A: The report includes all days, not just weekends.
incorrectExplanations.C: Real-time reporting is not supported; CUR updates are typically delayed.
incorrectExplanations.D: The report includes all AWS services, not just EC2, unless specifically filtered.

questions.question: Why does AWS ensure that Availability Zones within a Region are located in the same country?

options.text: To reduce storage costs by limiting international traffic
To improve instance launch speed across continents
To comply with data sovereignty laws requiring sensitive data to remain within a specific country
To ensure that all AWS services are automatically replicated worldwide

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. To comply with data sovereignty laws requiring sensitive data to remain within a specific country
questions.explanation: Data sovereignty refers to the legal requirement that certain data must be stored within the boundaries of a particular country. AWS designs its Availability Zones within a Region to be geographically separated (for fault tolerance) but still within the same country to help meet compliance requirements related to data privacy and storage.

incorrectExplanations.A: Cost savings are a factor, but data sovereignty is the main reason for same-country AZs.
incorrectExplanations.B: Launch speed is improved by proximity, but compliance is the key factor here.
incorrectExplanations.D: AWS services are not automatically replicated globally; replication must be configured.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of using a Content Delivery Network (CDN) such as Amazon CloudFront?

options.text: It encrypts all traffic within a private VPC by default
It stores user credentials in regional edge caches
It delivers content faster by caching it at edge locations closer to users
It provisions compute resources automatically across multiple regions

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. It delivers content faster by catching it at edge locations closer to users
questions.explanation: A CDN, like Amazon CloudFront, uses a network of edge locations and regional edge caches to serve content faster to users by caching it closer to their geographic location. This reduces latency and improves the overall performance of web applications.

incorrectExplanations.A: VPC-level encryption is unrelated to CDN functionality.
incorrectExplanations.B: CDNs do not store credentials—only static and dynamic content.
incorrectExplanations.D: CDNs do not provision compute resources—that’s handled by services like EC2 or Lambda.

questions.question: What is the purpose of having multiple Availability Zones within an AWS Region?

options.text: To ensure higher data compression for storage resources
To offer high availability, fault tolerance, and scalability through physically separated data centers
To allow users to deploy resources across different AWS accounts
To enable cross-account billing and automated backups

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. To offer high availability, fault tolerance, and scalability through physically separated data centers
questions.explanation: Each AWS Region consists of multiple Availability Zones, which are physically separated data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity. These zones are interconnected with low-latency, high-throughput networks, making it possible to build highly available and fault-tolerant applications.

incorrectExplanations.A: Data compression is unrelated to the purpose of Availability Zones.
incorrectExplanations.C: AZs are used for infrastructure resilience, not account separation.
incorrectExplanations.D: Cross-account billing and backups are managed by other AWS services, not through AZs.

questions.subtopic: Regions, Availability Zones and edge locations
questions.question: Which AWS infrastructure component is used by CloudFront to cache content closer to end-users for low-latency delivery?
questions.explanation: Edge locations are part of AWS’s global network of Points of Presence (PoPs) and are used by Amazon CloudFront to cache and deliver content to users with low latency. These locations are geographically distributed and help serve content faster from the nearest possible point.

incorrectExplanations.A: A Local Region is a full AWS datacenter but not specifically used for content caching.
incorrectExplanations.B: A Local Zone brings services closer to cities, but it’s not used for content delivery in CloudFront.
incorrectExplanations.D: Availability Zones are part of standard AWS Regions, not PoPs for caching.

questions.question: What is one benefit of Amazon Aurora's cloning feature?

options.text: It automatically converts the database engine to PostgreSQL during cloning
It allows quick and space-efficient duplication of a database, including sharing across AWS accounts
It disables backups on the cloned database to improve performance
It requires manual export and import of all database objects to perform cloning

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. It allows quick and space-efficient duplication of a database, including sharing across AWS accounts
questions.explanation: Amazon Aurora supports fast and efficient cloning of a database cluster. Clones use copy-on-write technology, which minimizes storage usage and speeds up the process. Aurora also allows sharing cloned databases with other AWS accounts, making testing and development easier.

incorrectExplanations.A: Aurora does not auto-convert engines during cloning—you must choose the same engine.
incorrectExplanations.C: Backups are not disabled during cloning; normal backup operations continue.
incorrectExplanations.D: Aurora cloning does not require manual export/import; it’s an automated process.

questions.question: What is a key characteristic of an Amazon Aurora cluster volume?

options.text: It stores data only in the primary Availability Zone to reduce replication overhead
It is a virtual storage volume that spans multiple Availability Zones with automatic data replication
It requires manual configuration to replicate data between regions
It can only support a single database engine per Region

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. It is a virtual storage volume that spans multiple Availability Zones with automatic data replication
questions.explanation: An Aurora cluster volume is a virtual storage layer designed for high availability and durability. It automatically replicates data across multiple Availability Zones in the same Region to ensure fault tolerance and fast recovery.

incorrectExplanations.A: Aurora replicates data across multiple AZs, not just one.
incorrectExplanations.C: Cross-AZ replication is automatic—you do not configure it manually.
incorrectExplanations.D: Aurora supports multiple engines (MySQL & PostgreSQL) within the same region.

questions.question: How does Amazon Aurora handle a failure in one of the disk volume segments that make up a cluster volume?

options.text: It automatically fails over to a new Region and deletes the failed volume
It stops the database cluster until the failed segment is manually replaced
It detects the failure, repairs the segment automatically, and uses data from other volumes to restore consistency
It sends a snapshot of the failed volume to S3 for archival and shuts down the cluster

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. It detects the failure, repairs the segment automatically, and uses data from other volumes to restore consistency
questions.explanation: Amazon Aurora is designed for high availability and fault tolerance. When a disk segment in the cluster volume fails, Aurora automatically repairs it using redundant data from other copies in the cluster volume. This ensures the repaired segment contains current and consistent data, without requiring manual intervention.

incorrectExplanations.A: Aurora does not need to migrate the database just for a disk failure—storage is already redundant across AZs.
incorrectExplanations.B: The engine does not restart or roll back due to storage segment failures.
incorrectExplanations.D: Aurora does not require manual snapshots or halt writes—repairs happen automatically and seamlessly.

questions.question: What is one of the main benefits of creating Aurora Replicas across multiple Availability Zones?

options.text: It allows automatic encryption of data at rest
It enables synchronous replication to reduce latency and improve backup reliability
It prevents the need for database snapshots during backups
It disables read traffic to ensure high write performance

questions.explanation: When Aurora Replicas are created in different Availability Zones, Amazon RDS synchronously replicates data from the primary DB instance. This provides high availability, data redundancy, and helps minimize I/O freezes and latency spikes during backups, making the system more resilient.

incorrectExplanations.A: Aurora does support encryption, but it's not related to the benefit of cross-AZ replication.
incorrectExplanations.C: Snapshots are still used for backups; replication helps improve performance during backups but doesn't replace snapshots.
incorrectExplanations.D: Read traffic is not disabled; Aurora Replicas are designed to offload read traffic from the primary instance.

technicalReview.reason: The explanation appears to conflate Aurora reader and storage replication. The source has no explicit key.

questions.question: How does Amazon Aurora ensure high availability and data durability across Availability Zones?

options.text: By replicating data to Amazon S3 in every Region
By maintaining 6 copies of data across 3 Availability Zones and automatically recovering in a healthy zone if needed
By creating daily snapshots and distributing them across Regions
By running only a single database instance to reduce complexity

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. By maintaining 6 copies of data across 3 Availability Zones and automatically recovering in a healthy zone if needed
questions.explanation: Amazon Aurora automatically maintains six copies of your data, with two copies in each of three different Availability Zones. If there’s a failure in one zone, Aurora can automatically recover using healthy copies from another zone without data loss, providing high availability and fault tolerance.

incorrectExplanations.A: Aurora does not replicate to S3 for database durability—S3 is a separate storage service.
incorrectExplanations.C: Snapshots are useful for backups but do not provide real-time fault tolerance.
incorrectExplanations.D: Aurora relies on replication and redundancy, not single-instance deployments, for high availability.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about instance store volumes in Amazon EC2?

options.text: They retain data even after the instance is stopped
They can be detached and reattached to other instances like EBS volumes
They are temporary storage volumes that are deleted when the instance is stopped or terminated
They support snapshot backups and are automatically encrypted

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. They are temporary storage volumes that are deleted when the instance is stopped or terminated
questions.explanation: Instance store volumes provide temporary block-level storage for an EC2 instance. The data is lost when the instance is stopped, terminated, or fails, making it suitable only for ephemeral data. In contrast, EBS-backed instances can be stopped and restarted without data loss.

incorrectExplanations.A: Instance store data is not persistent—it is deleted when the instance is stopped or terminated.
incorrectExplanations.B: Instance store volumes cannot be detached or reattached; they are tied to the host hardware.
incorrectExplanations.D: Instance store volumes do not support snapshots and are not automatically encrypted.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes Instance Store-backed EC2 instances?

options.text: They allow you to stop and restart the instance without losing data
They automatically back up all data to Amazon S3 on shutdown
They lose all data on the instance store volumes if the instance is terminated or fails
They support EBS volumes for persistent storage by default

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. They lose all data on the instance store volumes if the instance is terminated or fails
questions.explanation: Instance Store-backed EC2 instances use ephemeral storage directly attached to the physical host. This storage is not persistent, so any data stored is lost upon termination, failure, or hardware issues. Therefore, it's recommended to back up critical data regularly to persistent storage, like Amazon S3 or EBS.

incorrectExplanations.A: Instance store-backed instances cannot be stopped—only started or terminated.
incorrectExplanations.B: AWS does not automatically back up instance store data—you must do it manually.
incorrectExplanations.D: EBS volumes are not attached by default to instance store-backed instances; they're a separate storage type.

questions.question: Which AWS service is fully managed and is used to automate the creation, management, and deployment of Amazon Machine Images (AMIs)?
questions.explanation: EC2 Image Builder is a fully managed AWS service that simplifies the process of automating the creation, patching, testing, and distribution of Amazon Machine Images (AMIs). It helps ensure that your images are secure, up-to-date, and compliant with organizational standards.

incorrectExplanations.A: AWS CodeDeploy is used for automated application deployments, not AMI creation.
incorrectExplanations.B: EC2 Auto Scaling launches instances from existing AMIs but does not manage or create them.
incorrectExplanations.D: Session Manager provides secure shell access to EC2 instances, not image creation capabilities.

questions.question: What is a key benefit of using Reserved Instances in Amazon EC2?

options.text: They automatically scale based on incoming traffic without user configuration
They allow you to pause billing when the instance is idle
They offer a lower hourly rate in exchange for committing to a one- or three-year term
They support instant switching between Regions without reconfiguration

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. They offer a lower hourly rate in exchange for committing to a one- or three-year term
questions.explanation: Reserved Instances (RIs) allow you to make a low, upfront payment and commit to using an instance for a 1-year or 3-year term, in return for a significantly reduced hourly rate compared to On-Demand pricing. AWS offers Standard and Convertible RI classes, with Convertible RIs allowing instance type changes

incorrectExplanations.A: Auto scaling is handled by Auto Scaling Groups, not Reserved Instances.
incorrectExplanations.B: Billing for RIs is continuous over the term; there is no pause.
incorrectExplanations.D: RIs are tied to a specific Region, and switching requires modification or exchange in case of Convertible RIs.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes data durability in services like Amazon S3?

options.text: Data is stored in a single Availability Zone for faster retrieval
Data is replicated across multiple Availability Zones to achieve 99.999999999% durability
Durability ensures that data can only be accessed by the root user
Durability guarantees that deleted data can be recovered for 30 days

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. Data is replicated across multiple Availability Zones to achieve 99.999999999% durability
questions.explanation: Durability measures how reliably your data is stored over time. Amazon S3 achieves 11 nines (99.999999999%) durability by automatically replicating data across multiple Availability Zones, ensuring it is not lost even in the case of component or AZ failures.

incorrectExplanations.A:
Data is stored in a single Availability Zone for faster retrieval
This is incorrect because durability relies on multi-AZ replication. Storing data in a single AZ increases the risk of loss in case of failure.
incorrectExplanations.C:
Durability ensures that data can only be accessed by the root user
This is false. Access control is managed by IAM policies and bucket permissions, not by durability.
incorrectExplanations.D:
Durability guarantees that deleted data can be recovered for 30 days
This is incorrect. Once data is deleted (unless versioning or a lifecycle policy like S3 Object Lock is used), durability does not apply. Durability is about protecting data while it exists, not restoring deleted items.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the regional nature of Amazon ECS (Elastic Container Service)?

options.text: ECS resources are automatically replicated across all AWS Regions
ECS is a regional service, meaning clusters and tasks are specific to the AWS Region in which they are created
ECS tasks run globally and are not tied to any specific Region
ECS uses Availability Zones instead of Regions to manage container placement

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. ECS is a regional service, meaning clusters and tasks are specific to the AWS Region in which they are created.
questions.explanation: Amazon ECS is a regional service. This means that clusters, services, and tasks you create in ECS are scoped to the Region in which you provision them. Resources are not automatically replicated across Regions, and you must configure deployments separately for each Region if needed

incorrectExplanations.A: ECS does not replicate resources across Regions automatically; this must be done manually.
incorrectExplanations.C: ECS tasks are tied to the Region in which the ECS cluster resides.
incorrectExplanations.D: ECS does consider Availability Zones for task placement within a Region, but the service is defined at the regional level, not zonal.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the role of a container image in a containerized application?

options.text: It is a temporary file system that stores application logs during runtime
It is a read-only template that includes everything needed to run an application
It is a database snapshot used for container storage
It stores environment variables for runtime configuration only

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. It is a read-only template that includes everything needed to run an application
questions.explanation: A container image is a read-only template used to create containers. It includes everything required to run the application: the application code, runtime, system tools, system libraries, and dependencies. Containers launched from the image use this consistent environment for execution.

incorrectExplanations.A: The file system during runtime is writable, but the image itself is read-only and doesn't store logs.
incorrectExplanations.C: Container images are not database snapshots; they define the environment for the app.
incorrectExplanations.D: While containers may use environment variables, images contain the full application stack, not just configs.

questions.question: What is a key feature of Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS)?

options.text: It stores large volumes of structured data for analytics
It uses the publish-subscribe model and pushes notifications to subscribers
It provides a database engine for mobile app backends
It requires clients to poll regularly for new messages

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. It uses the publish-subscribe model and pushes notifications to subscribers
questions.explanation: Amazon SNS is a fully managed messaging service that supports the publish-subscribe (pub-sub) model. Publishers send messages to a topic, and subscribers (such as email, SMS, Lambda, or SQS endpoints) receive the messages via a push mechanism, eliminating the need for polling.

incorrectExplanations.A: SNS is not designed for data storage or analytics—it's a messaging service.
incorrectExplanations.C: SNS is not a database; it's used for event-driven notifications.
incorrectExplanations.D: SNS uses push notifications, not polling.

questions.question: Which AWS service allows you to send push notifications such as email and SMS messages to individuals or groups?
questions.explanation: Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) is a fully managed messaging service that supports push-based delivery of messages via email, SMS (text messaging), mobile push, and more. It allows messages to be sent to individuals or entire groups through topics.

incorrectExplanations.A: Amazon S3 is a storage service, not a messaging system.
incorrectExplanations.B: Amazon EC2 provides compute resources, not messaging.
incorrectExplanations.D: Amazon RDS is used for relational databases, not for sending notifications.

questions.question: Which AWS service allows you to configure automatic scaling using scaling plans that include both dynamic and predictive scaling?
questions.explanation: AWS Auto Scaling enables you to automatically scale your AWS resources (such as EC2 instances, ECS services, DynamoDB tables, etc.) using scaling plans. These plans can include both dynamic scaling (based on real-time demand) and predictive scaling (based on historical trends and machine learning).

incorrectExplanations.B: AWS CloudTrail is used for logging API activity, not scaling resources.
incorrectExplanations.C: Amazon EC2 provides compute instances, but does not handle scaling plans directly.
incorrectExplanations.D: AWS Config tracks resource configuration history, not scaling.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of an Auto Scaling Group in Amazon EC2?

options.text: To assign unique IAM roles to each instance in your VPC
To group EC2 instances with different configurations for auditing
To manage a group of EC2 instances with similar characteristics for automated scaling and health monitoring
To migrate EC2 instances between Regions for disaster recovery

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. To manage a group of EC2 instances with similar characteristics for automated scaling and health monitoring
questions.explanation: An Auto Scaling Group (ASG) allows you to define and manage a collection of EC2 instances that share the same configuration. It helps automatically scale the number of instances up or down based on demand and ensures that healthy instances are maintained according to the desired count.

incorrectExplanations.A: IAM roles are not managed at the group level in an ASG.
incorrectExplanations.B: ASGs manage instances with similar, not different, configurations.
incorrectExplanations.D: ASGs are region-specific and do not handle cross-region migrations.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a launch template in an Auto Scaling Group?

options.text: To configure security group rules for the entire VPC
To automate the patching of EC2 instances across Regions
To define configuration details such as AMI ID, instance type, and security groups for EC2 instances
To replicate EC2 instances into S3 buckets for backup

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. To define configuration details such as AMI ID, instance type, and security groups for EC2 instances
questions.explanation: A launch template is used to define the EC2 instance configuration—including the Amazon Machine Image (AMI), instance type, key pair, block device mappings, and security groups. It allows consistent, repeatable deployment of instances, especially in Auto Scaling Groups.

incorrectExplanations.A: Security group rules are managed separately, not through launch templates.
incorrectExplanations.B: Launch templates don’t automate patching; AWS Systems Manager is used for that.
incorrectExplanations.D: EC2 instances aren’t replicated into S3 via launch templates; Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) are used for backup purposes.

questions.question: What is a launch configuration used for in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group?

options.text: To schedule instance backups across multiple regions
To monitor the performance of running EC2 instances
To define the configuration details for EC2 instances launched by the Auto Scaling group
To apply IAM policies to users accessing the EC2 Dashboard

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. To define the configuration details for EC2 instances launched by the Auto Scaling group
questions.explanation: A launch configuration is a template that defines how EC2 instances should be configured when launched by an Auto Scaling group. It includes settings such as the AMI ID, instance type, key pair, security groups, and block device mapping. Although AWS now recommends launch templates, launch configurations are still supported.

incorrectExplanations.A: Backup scheduling is not handled by launch configurations.
incorrectExplanations.B: Monitoring is done through CloudWatch, not launch configurations.
incorrectExplanations.D: IAM policy application is unrelated to instance configuration templates.

technicalReview.reason: This uses legacy launch configurations, subject to current restrictions for accounts and instance types.

questions.question: What is the primary function of CloudTrail Lake in AWS?

options.text: It provides real-time monitoring for EC2 instance metrics
It allows aggregation, immutable storage, and querying of activity logs
It automatically deletes old logs to save storage space
It replicates IAM roles across AWS accounts

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. It allows aggregation, immutable storage, and querying of activity logs
questions.explanation: CloudTrail Lake is a managed data lake feature in AWS CloudTrail that enables users to aggregate, store immutably, and query activity logs across AWS accounts and Regions. It supports querying through the AWS SDK, CLI, and console, making it easier to analyze user and service activity.

incorrectExplanations.A: Real-time monitoring of instance metrics is handled by Amazon CloudWatch, not CloudTrail Lake.
incorrectExplanations.C: CloudTrail Lake retains logs immutably; they are not auto-deleted for cost savings.
incorrectExplanations.D: IAM role replication across accounts is not a feature of CloudTrail Lake.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about creating an organization trail in AWS CloudTrail?

options.text: It can be created by any account within the AWS Organization
It only logs events from the management account by default
It must be created in the management account and logs events across all member accounts
It is limited to a single Availability Zone

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. It must be created in the management account and log events across all member accounts
questions.explanation: An organization trail in AWS CloudTrail allows you to log all events across all accounts in an AWS Organization. However, only the management account has the permission to create and manage organization trials. Once created, it captures events from every account in the organization.

incorrectExplanations.A: Only the management account can create an organization trial.
incorrectExplanations.B: It captures events from all accounts, not just the management account.
incorrectExplanations.D: Trails are global or regional, not tied to an Availability Zone.

questions.question: What happens automatically in Amazon Route 53 after you successfully register a domain name?

options.text: A private hosted zone is created and linked to your VPC
The domain is locked for editing for 30 days
A public hosted zone is created with the same name as the registered domain
An SSL certificate is issued for the domain

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. A public hosted zone is created with the same name as the registered domain
questions.explanation: When you register a domain using Amazon Route 53, it automatically creates a public hosted zone with the same name as the domain. This hosted zone includes default DNS records (such as name servers and start of authority) to help you begin managing DNS immediately.

incorrectExplanations.A: Private hosted zones must be created manually and are used with Amazon VPCs, not automatically set up on domain registration.
incorrectExplanations.B: There is no 30-day lock for editing DNS settings after domain registration in Route 53.
incorrectExplanations.D: SSL certificates are managed separately (e.g., via AWS Certificate Manager), not automatically issued upon registration.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an alias record in Amazon Route 53?

options.text: To create temporary DNS redirects for testing
To route traffic to non-AWS domains using CNAME records
To route traffic directly to AWS resources like S3 buckets or CloudFront distributions
To encrypt DNS queries between hosted zones

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. To route traffic directly to AWS resources like S3 buckets or CloudFront distributions
questions.explanation: Alias records in Route 53 are special types of DNS records that let you route traffic to AWS resources, such as Amazon S3 buckets, CloudFront distributions, Elastic Load Balancers, and API Gateway endpoints, without needing to use an IP address or a CNAME at the zone apex.

incorrectExplanations.A: Alias records are not for temporary use or testing; they’re used for production routing.
incorrectExplanations.B: Alias records are used for AWS-managed destinations, not external domains.
incorrectExplanations.D: DNS encryption is not handled by alias records but by services like DNS over HTTPS (DoH) or TLS at the application layer.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the Simple Routing Policy in Amazon Route 53?

options.text: It routes traffic based on user location to the nearest endpoint
It splits traffic randomly across multiple AWS Regions
It routes internet traffic to a single resource and allows multiple values in one record, such as multiple IPs
It automatically adjusts traffic routing based on resource health checks

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. It routes internet traffic to a single resource and allows multiple values in one record, such as multiple Ips
questions.explanation: The Simple Routing Policy is the most basic routing type in Route 53. It routes traffic to a single resource, such as a web server or an S3 website endpoint. While you cannot create multiple records with the same name and type, you can provide multiple values (like multiple IPs) in the same record.

incorrectExplanations.A: That describes Geolocation or Latency-based routing, not simple routing.
incorrectExplanations.B: Weighted routing policy is used to split traffic, not simple routing.
incorrectExplanations.D: Health checks can be associated with simple routing, but failover routing is specifically designed for health-based traffic redirection.

questions.question: Which of the following programming languages are natively supported by AWS Lambda? (Choose all that apply)
questions.sourceAnswerKey:
A. Node.js
B. Java
C. C#
E. Go
F. Python
G. Ruby
H. PowerShell
questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda provides native runtime support for the following languages:
Node.js
Java
C# (via .NET Core)
Go
Python
Ruby
PowerShell (via .NET Core for Windows scripting)
PHP is not natively supported, but can be run using custom runtimes via AWS Lambda’s Lambda Runtime API.

questions.question: What best describes a function in AWS Lambda?

options.text: A container image that manages VPC networking
A monitoring tool for tracking AWS usage and billing
A script or program that processes events and returns a response
A physical server that runs user-defined software

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. A script or program that processes events and returns a response
questions.explanation: In AWS Lambda, a function is your application logic—a script or program written in a supported language (e.g., Python, Node.js, Java). When Lambda is invoked, it passes an event to the function, which executes the code and optionally returns a response.

incorrectExplanations.A: Lambda functions may use containers, but this refers to deployment packaging, not the function itself.
incorrectExplanations.B: AWS Billing and Cost Explorer tools monitor usage—not Lambda.
incorrectExplanations.D: Lambda is a serverless service, meaning users don’t manage physical servers.

questions.question: Which of the following are true about AWS Lambda layers? (Choose 2 answers)

options.text: Layers allow you to package and share libraries or dependencies across multiple Lambda functions
Layers are used to store function execution logs in CloudWatch
Layers help separate in-development code from stable dependencies
Layers are required for running Lambda functions in VPCs
Layers automatically replicate function code across multiple Regions

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
A. Layers allow you to package and share libraries or dependencies across multiple Lambda functions
C. Layers help separate in-development code from stable dependencies
questions.explanation:
Lambda layers are a mechanism for sharing libraries, custom runtimes, and dependencies across multiple Lambda functions.
They help manage code more efficiently by separating changing function code from stable or reusable components.

incorrectExplanations.B: Logs are stored in CloudWatch, but layers are not used for logging.
incorrectExplanations.D: Layers are not required for VPC access; VPC configuration is separate.
incorrectExplanations.E: Layers are Region-specific and do not automatically replicate across Regions.

questions.question: You are setting up a site-to-site VPN to securely connect your on-premises data center to your AWS VPC. Which component should you attach to your VPC to act as the VPN concentrator on the AWS side of the connection?
questions.explanation: A Virtual Private Gateway (VGW) is the VPN endpoint on the AWS side of a site-to-site VPN. It enables secure communication between your on-premises data center and your VPC over an IPsec VPN tunnel.

incorrectExplanations.A: Internet Gateway allows public internet access, not VPN connectivity.
incorrectExplanations.B: NAT Gateway enables instances in a private subnet to access the internet, not for VPN use.
incorrectExplanations.D: VPC Peering is used for connecting two VPCs, not on-premises networks.

questions.question: What is the primary use of AWS PrivateLink?

options.text: To connect VPCs across Regions using public IPs
To privately connect your VPC to AWS services and partner services without using public internet
To manage IAM policies across multiple AWS accounts
To automatically assign public IP addresses to EC2 instances in private subnets

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. To privately connect your VPC to AWS services and partner services without using public internet
questions.explanation: AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity between your VPC and supported AWS services, services in other AWS accounts, or AWS Marketplace partner services without exposing traffic to the public internet. It uses interface VPC endpoints powered by Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs).

incorrectExplanations.A:
To connect VPCs across Regions using public IPs
This describes VPC Peering or Transit Gateway with inter-region support, not PrivateLink. PrivateLink does not use public IPs or support cross-region VPC-to-VPC peering.
incorrectExplanations.C:
To manage IAM policies across multiple AWS accounts
This relates to AWS Organizations or Resource Access Manager (RAM), not PrivateLink. IAM policy management is outside the scope of networking services.
incorrectExplanations.D:
To automatically assign public IP addresses to EC2 instances in private subnets
This is a function of Auto-assign public IP settings in subnet configuration and has no relation to PrivateLink, which is used for private connectivity.

questions.question: You have a VPC with both public and private subnets. You want instances in the private subnet to access the internet for software updates, but you do not want them to be reachable from the internet. Which of the following should you use?

options.text: NAT Gateway in a public subnet
Egress-Only Internet Gateway in a public subnet

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. NAT Gateway in a public subnet
questions.explanation: A NAT Gateway enables instances in a private subnet to initiate outbound traffic to the internet, such as downloading software updates, while preventing inbound connections from the internet. The NAT Gateway itself must reside in a public subnet with a route to the Internet Gateway.

incorrectExplanations.A:
Internet Gateway
Provides direct internet access to instances in a public subnet, but cannot be used alone by instances in a private subnet.
incorrectExplanations.C:
VPC Peering Connection
Used to connect two VPCs privately, not to access the internet.
incorrectExplanations.D:
Egress-Only Internet Gateway in a public subnet
Only supports IPv6 traffic and is not suitable for IPv4-based internet access typically used for software updates.

questions.question:
Which of the following IP addresses in an AWS subnet CIDR block are reserved and cannot be assigned to instances?
(Choose all that apply)

options.text: The first IP address in the CIDR block
The second IP address in the CIDR block
The third IP address in the CIDR block
The last IP address in the CIDR block
Any IP address not in the reserved range
The fifth IP address in the CIDR block

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
A. The first IP address
B. The second IP address
C. The third IP address
D. The last IP address
F. The fifth IP address
questions.explanation:
In every AWS subnet, five IP addresses are reserved and cannot be assigned to EC2 instances:
First IP – Network address
Second IP – VPC router
Third IP – Reserved for AWS DNS
Fourth IP – Reserved for future use (by AWS)
Last IP – Network broadcast address (though AWS does not support broadcast)
So in a /24 subnet like 192.168.1.0/24, the IPs 192.168.1.0, .1, .2, .3, and .255 are reserved.

incorrectExplanations.E:
Any IP address not in the reserved range
This is not correct to select, because it refers to assignable IPs. The question asked for reserved ones.

technicalReview.reason: The source key selects the fifth address. The source explanation and AWS IPv4 subnet documentation identify the fourth address instead.

questions.question: You are managing two VPCs: VPC-A (requester) and VPC-B (accepter), which are in a pending-acceptance peering state. You realise that VPC-A needs to add a new CIDR block. What is the correct sequence of actions you should take to comply with AWS peering rules?

options.text: Add the CIDR block directly to VPC-A while the peering connection is pending
Ask the owner of VPC-B to accept the peering connection, then add the CIDR block to VPC-A
Delete the peering request from VPC-A, add the CIDR block, and then create a new peering request
Add the CIDR block to both VPCs at the same time without deleting the peering connection

questions.sourceAnswerKey: C. Delete the peering request from VPC-A, add the CIDR block, and then create a new peering request
questions.explanation: In a pending-acceptance state, the requester VPC (VPC-A) is not allowed to add CIDR blocks. The only way to proceed is to delete the pending peering request, add the CIDR block, and then re-initiate the peering connection.

incorrectExplanations.A: You cannot add CIDR blocks to the requester VPC in a pending-acceptance state
incorrectExplanations.B: Even if VPC-B accepts the connection, you won’t be able to add the CIDR if the request wasn't updated
incorrectExplanations.D: Simultaneous CIDR block additions are not allowed and may result in overlapping CIDR conflicts

questions.question: Which AWS service provides a resource inventory, configuration history, and change notifications to support security and governance?
questions.explanation: AWS Config is a fully managed service that lets you track changes to AWS resources, maintain a resource inventory, record configuration history, and receive notifications about changes. It's widely used for auditing, compliance, and governance.

incorrectExplanations.A: AWS CloudTrail tracks API activity, not detailed configuration history or resource inventory
incorrectExplanations.C: AWS Systems Manager helps manage infrastructure but does not track configuration changes
incorrectExplanations.D: AWS Inspector is used for automated security assessments, not configuration tracking

questions.question: Which of the following statements are true about Amazon Aurora? (Choose 2 answers)

options.text: It is a fully managed relational database engine compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL
It is used only for storing NoSQL documents
It provides automatic failover, replication, and backup
It is a self-managed service that requires customer patching and maintenance

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
A. It is a fully managed relational database engine compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL
C. It provides automatic failover, replication, and backup
questions.explanation:
A. Amazon Aurora is designed to be compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL, allowing applications using these engines to easily migrate.
C. Aurora supports high availability through replication, automatic failover, and automated backups as part of its managed service.

incorrectExplanations.B: Aurora is not a NoSQL service; it's a relational database engine.
incorrectExplanations.D: Aurora is fully managed by AWS; customers do not handle patching or maintenance.
incorrectExplanations.E: Aurora supports both MySQL and PostgreSQL, not just PostgreSQL.

questions.question: Which AWS tool helps you evaluate and improve your cloud architecture by answering a set of best-practice questions?
questions.explanation: The AWS Well-Architected Tool helps you review and improve your cloud workloads by evaluating them against AWS best practices across six pillars (e.g., security, reliability, performance efficiency). You answer evaluation questions to identify risks and areas for improvement.

incorrectExplanations.A: AWS Trusted Advisor provides checks for cost, security, and service limits, but doesn’t offer architecture reviews.
incorrectExplanations.C: AWS Config tracks configuration changes, not architectural design reviews.
incorrectExplanations.D: AWS Budgets is used to monitor and control AWS spending, not architecture best practices.

questions.question: Which of the following is not one of the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
questions.explanation:
