The six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework are:
Security
Reliability
Performance Efficiency
Operational Excellence
Cost Optimization
Sustainability
Automation is a technique used within several pillars but is not a pillar by itself.

incorrectExplanations.A: Security is one of the core pillars focused on data protection and access control.
incorrectExplanations.B: Cost Optimization aims to run systems efficiently while reducing unnecessary expenses.
incorrectExplanations.D: Sustainability was added as the sixth pillar to help organizations reduce their environmental impact.

questions.question: What is the main objective of the Security Pillar in the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

options.text: To optimise resource usage and reduce cloud costs
To assess and mitigate risks while protecting data, systems, and assets
To improve application performance across regions
To deploy applications as fast as possible

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. To assess and mitigate risks while protecting data, systems, and assets
questions.explanation: The Security Pillar focuses on implementing measures that protect information, systems, and assets, using risk assessments and mitigation strategies. This helps deliver business value securely and reliably.

incorrectExplanations.A: Refers to the Cost Optimization pillar, not security.
incorrectExplanations.C: Linked to the Performance Efficiency pillar.
incorrectExplanations.D: Emphasised in the Operational Excellence pillar, not security.

questions.question: Which of the following are true about Amazon EBS snapshots? (Choose 2 answers)

options.text: EBS snapshots are automatically deleted when the instance is terminated
Snapshots are stored in Amazon S3
You can create point-in-time snapshots of EBS volumes
Snapshots cannot be copied to other AWS Regions

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
B. Snapshots are stored in Amazon S3
C. You can create point-in-time snapshots of EBS volumes
questions.explanation:
B. EBS snapshots are persisted to Amazon S3, though not directly visible in your S3 bucket.
C. Snapshots provide point-in-time backups of EBS volumes, which can be used to restore or create new volumes.

incorrectExplanations.A: Snapshots are not deleted when the instance is terminated — they persist independently.
incorrectExplanations.D: Snapshots can be copied across AWS regions for backup, migration, or disaster recovery.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Amazon EBS snapshots are correct? (Choose 2 answers)

options.text: Snapshots are persisted to Amazon S3 storage
Snapshots can be copied across AWS Regions
Snapshots are deleted automatically when an instance stops
Snapshots are stored in your S3 bucket and visible by default

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
A. Snapshots are persisted to Amazon S3 storage
B. Snapshots can be copied across AWS Regions
questions.explanation:
A. Amazon EBS snapshots are persisted to Amazon S3, although not directly accessible like typical S3 objects.
B. EBS snapshots can be copied across regions, supporting backup, disaster recovery, and migration use cases.

incorrectExplanations.C: Snapshots are not automatically deleted when an instance stops or terminates — they remain until manually deleted.
incorrectExplanations.D: While stored in S3, snapshots are not visible in your S3 bucket and are managed through the EBS console or API, not the S3 interface.

questions.question: Which of the following performance metrics provided by Amazon CloudWatch can help you monitor and optimise Amazon EBS volumes? (Choose 2 answers)
questions.explanation:
A. Bandwidth measures the amount of data transferred over time, helping assess if your volume throughput meets application needs.
C. Latency reflects the time it takes to complete I/O operations, helping detect bottlenecks.

incorrectExplanations.B: Route propagation relates to networking (e.g., route tables in VPC), not EBS volume performance.
incorrectExplanations.D: Availability Zone name is a location attribute, not a performance metric.

questions.question: Which of the following are true about AWS Backup? (Choose 2 answers)

options.text: AWS Backup is an automated and centralized backup service for AWS resources
AWS Backup supports backups for Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon RDS
AWS Backup replaces the need for IAM policies when securing backups
AWS Backup is used only for Amazon S3 buckets

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
A. AWS Backup is an automated and centralized backup service for AWS resources
B. AWS Backup supports backups for Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon RDS
questions.explanation:
A. AWS Backup provides a centralized and automated way to manage backups across multiple AWS services.
B. It integrates with services like Amazon EBS, Amazon RDS, Amazon EFS, Amazon DynamoDB, and AWS Storage Gateway to simplify backup management.

incorrectExplanations.C: AWS Backup does not eliminate the need for IAM policies; IAM is still required to manage permissions for backup operations.
incorrectExplanations.D: AWS Backup is not limited to S3 — in fact, it does not natively back up S3 objects; S3 has its own versioning and replication options.

questions.question: Which of the following are true about a multi-region trail in AWS CloudTrail? (Choose 2 answers)

options.text: It records events from all AWS regions
It stores logs only in the default region where the trail was created
It delivers event log files to an S3 bucket that you specify
It can only be enabled through the AWS CLI

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
A. It records events from all AWS regions
C. It delivers event log files to an S3 bucket that you specify
questions.explanation:
A. A multi-region trail captures API events from all AWS regions, improving governance and compliance visibility across global resources.
C. You can specify an S3 bucket to store the log files generated by the trail, regardless of the region in which the events occurred.

incorrectExplanations.B: Multi-region trails do not restrict logs to the default region — they collect from all regions.
incorrectExplanations.D: While the AWS CLI can be used to enable trails, the AWS Console also fully supports this (it's the default method for most users).

questions.question: In AWS CloudTrail, what is the term used to describe a record of activity performed by a user, role, or service?
questions.explanation: In AWS CloudTrail, an event represents a record of an activity that occurred in your AWS account. This activity may be an API call made by a user, an IAM role, or an AWS service.

incorrectExplanations.A: Audit log is a general term but not the specific object used in CloudTrail
incorrectExplanations.C: Snapshot refers to EBS or RDS backups, not activity logs
incorrectExplanations.D: Resource action is not a defined CloudTrail concept

questions.question: Which of the following are true about Amazon SNS mobile and messaging notifications? (Choose 2 answers)

options.text: SNS supports sending push notifications to mobile devices like iOS and Android
SNS can only send messages to devices located in the United States
SNS can fan out messages to multiple protocols such as SMS and email
SNS only supports HTTP-based delivery and not email or SMS

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
A. SNS supports sending push notifications to mobile devices like iOS and Android
C. SNS can fan out messages to multiple protocols such as SMS and email
questions.explanation:
A. Amazon SNS allows mobile push notifications to platforms like iOS, Android, Fire OS, Windows, and Baidu.
C. SNS uses the fan-out pattern to deliver the same message to multiple endpoints such as SMS, email (SMTP), mobile push, and HTTP/S.

incorrectExplanations.B: SNS supports SMS delivery to 200+ countries, not just the U.S.
incorrectExplanations.D: SNS supports multiple protocols including email and SMS, not only HTTP.

questions.question: Which of the following statements are true about Standard and Convertible Reserved Instances? (Choose 2 answers)

options.text: Standard Reserved Instances offer the highest discount but allow limited modifications
Convertible Reserved Instances can be exchanged for different attributes
Convertible Reserved Instances can be sold on the Reserved Instance Marketplace
Standard Reserved Instances cannot be sold during their term

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
A. Standard Reserved Instances offer the highest discount but allow limited modifications
B. Convertible Reserved Instances can be exchanged for different attributes
questions.explanation:
A. Standard RIs provide higher discounts but allow limited changes and can be sold on the Reserved Instance Marketplace.
B. Convertible RIs allow you to exchange them for other Convertible RIs with different attributes (e.g., instance type, OS).

incorrectExplanations.C: Convertible RIs cannot be sold on the Reserved Instance Marketplace.
incorrectExplanations.D: Standard RIs can be sold on the marketplace after a 30-day hold period.

questions.question: Which of the following are true about AWS security groups used as firewalls? (Choose 2 answers)

options.text: Security groups allow you to specify allowed inbound and outbound traffic by protocol and port
Security groups are stateless, requiring separate rules for inbound and outbound traffic
Security groups act at the instance level, not the subnet level
Security groups block all traffic by default, including outbound traffic

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
A. Security groups allow you to specify allowed inbound and outbound traffic by protocol and port
C. Security groups act at the instance level, not the subnet level
questions.explanation:
A. You can configure security groups to allow traffic based on protocol, port range, and source/destination IPs.
C. Security groups are associated with EC2 instances, not entire subnets like network ACLs.

incorrectExplanations.B: Security groups are stateful, meaning if you allow inbound traffic, return traffic is automatically allowed.
incorrectExplanations.D: By default, security groups allow all outbound traffic, but no inbound traffic.

questions.subtopic: Regions, Availability Zones and edge locations
questions.question: Which of the following are true about AWS Regions and Availability Zones? (Choose 2 answers)

options.text: A Region consists of multiple isolated Availability Zones
All Availability Zones within a Region share the same data center
You can deploy AWS resources such as EC2 and EBS in specific Availability Zones
AWS guarantees zero latency between Availability Zones in the same Region

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
A. A Region consists of multiple isolated Availability Zones
C. You can deploy AWS resources such as EC2 and EBS in specific Availability Zones
questions.explanation:
A. Each AWS Region is a geographically distinct area and includes multiple AZs for fault tolerance and availability.
C. You can choose specific AZs for deploying resources like EC2 instances and EBS volumes to improve performance or redundancy.

incorrectExplanations.B: AZs are physically separated data centers within a Region, not shared.
incorrectExplanations.D: While AZs are connected by low-latency, high-bandwidth networking, zero latency is not guaranteed.

questions.question: Which of the following are true about On-Demand Instances in AWS EC2? (Choose 2 answers)

options.text: On-Demand Instances require long-term contracts and upfront payments
They help eliminate the need to purchase and manage physical hardware
On-Demand Instances are ideal for applications with steady, predictable usage
They are suitable for unpredictable workloads or short-term, spiky traffic

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
B. They help eliminate the need to purchase and manage physical hardware
D. They are suitable for unpredictable workloads or short-term, spiky traffic
questions.explanation:
B. On-Demand Instances allow you to run workloads without managing hardware, offering flexibility and speed.
D. They are ideal for unpredictable or bursty workloads, as you pay by the hour or second without long-term commitments.

incorrectExplanations.A: On-Demand Instances do not require long-term contracts or upfront payments.
incorrectExplanations.C: For steady, predictable workloads, Reserved Instances are typically more cost-effective than On-Demand.

questions.subtopic: Variable expenses and economies of scale
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the AWS cloud benefit of trading capital expense for variable expense?

options.text: You commit to a 3-year pricing model for reserved resources
You only pay for the compute resources you use, eliminating upfront investments
You purchase and manage servers in your on-premises data centre
You pay the same monthly fee regardless of usage

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. You only pay for the compute resources you use, eliminating upfront investments
questions.explanation: This benefit refers to replacing upfront capital investment in hardware with pay-as-you-go pricing, which is one of the foundational economic advantages of cloud computing. AWS lets you scale resources up or down and only charges for what you use.

incorrectExplanations.A: Describes Reserved Instances, which involve commitment, not variable pricing
incorrectExplanations.C: It is the opposite of cloud-based resource provisioning
incorrectExplanations.D: A flat monthly fee doesn't reflect the usage-based billing model of AWS

questions.question: What is the purpose of an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) in AWS?

options.text: It stores encrypted S3 data for backup
It packages the operating system and custom software into a reusable template
It monitors EC2 instance performance using CloudWatch
It acts as a firewall controlling access to EC2 instances

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. It packages the operating system and custom software into a reusable template
questions.explanation: An Amazon Machine Image (AMI) provides a blueprint for launching EC2 instances. It includes the OS, application server, and custom configurations, allowing you to create multiple identical instances.

incorrectExplanations.A: Refers to Amazon S3 backups, not AMIs
incorrectExplanations.C: CloudWatch is used for monitoring, not creating instance templates
incorrectExplanations.D: Security groups or network ACLs manage access control, not AMIs

questions.question: Which of the following EC2 instance types are correctly matched with their optimization category? (Choose 2 answers)
questions.sourceAnswerKey:
B. m-type – General purpose
D. p-type – Accelerated computing
questions.explanation:
B. m-type and t-type are general purpose instances, offering a balance of compute, memory, and networking.
D. p-type, g-type, and f-type are designed for accelerated computing using GPUs or FPGAs.

incorrectExplanations.A: c-type is for compute-optimized, not memory
incorrectExplanations.C: r-type is for memory-optimized, not storage; storage-optimized types include i-type, d-type, and h-type

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a containerized application?

options.text: An application that is deployed directly onto a physical server without any abstraction
An application that runs in a lightweight, portable environment containing code, dependencies, and runtime
An application hosted only in Amazon EC2 without scalability
An application that requires a dedicated database per deployment

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. An application that runs in a lightweight, portable environment containing code, dependencies, and runtime
questions.explanation: Containers package everything an application needs to run: code, runtime, libraries, and dependencies. This allows them to run consistently across environments, making them ideal for microservices and modern cloud-native applications.

incorrectExplanations.A: Describes bare metal deployments, not containers
incorrectExplanations.C: Containers can run on EC2, but are not limited to it and are inherently scalable
incorrectExplanations.D: Dedicated databases are not a requirement for containerized apps

questions.question: Which of the following statements are true about building and storing container images in AWS? (Choose 2 answers)

options.text: Images are built from a Docker file that defines all required components
Container images can only be stored locally and cannot be shared
Images can be stored in a registry for reuse across clusters
Docker files are binary files used to launch EC2 instances directly

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
A. Images are built from a Docker file that defines all required components
C. Images can be stored in a registry for reuse across clusters
questions.explanation:
A. A Docker file is a text file that includes instructions to build a container image (e.g., base OS, dependencies, and commands).
C. Built container images can be stored in a container registry like Amazon ECR (Elastic Container Registry) for deployment and reuse.

incorrectExplanations.B: Container images can be stored and shared via registries like ECR, Docker Hub, etc.
incorrectExplanations.D: Docker files are text-based and not used to launch EC2 instances directly — they build images for containers.

questions.question: What AWS service provides a private container image registry for storing and managing Docker images?
questions.explanation: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR) is a fully managed Docker container registry that allows AWS users to store, manage, and deploy container images. Each AWS account has its own private registry, and users can create repositories within it to store images.

incorrectExplanations.A: Amazon ECS is a container orchestration service, not a registry
incorrectExplanations.B: Amazon EKS is for Kubernetes orchestration, not image storage
incorrectExplanations.D: AWS Lambda runs functions, not container registries

questions.question: What must be done before an IAM user can create or manage resources in Amazon ECR?

options.text: Enable ECR in the IAM dashboard
Attach an appropriate IAM policy granting ECR permissions
Use the root account to access ECR features
Create an EC2 instance and configure ECR access from there

questions.sourceAnswerKey: B. Attach an appropriate IAM policy granting ECR permissions
questions.explanation: By default, IAM users do not have access to manage Amazon ECR resources. You must explicitly assign IAM policies (e.g., AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryFullAccess) to allow the user to perform tasks using the ECR API or console.

incorrectExplanations.A: ECR permissions are not "enabled" from the IAM dashboard — they are granted via policies
incorrectExplanations.C: Using the root account is not a recommended security practice
incorrectExplanations.D: EC2 instances can use ECR, but IAM users still need explicit permissions

questions.question: A Cloud Practitioner is building a new application and wants to integrate AWS service features directly into the application code. Which of the following is the most appropriate tool for this purpose?
questions.explanation: The AWS SDK allows developers to interact with AWS services directly from within their code using programming languages like Python, Java, and JavaScript. This makes it the most suitable tool for embedding AWS functionality into applications.

incorrectExplanations.A: AWS CLI: Suitable for command-line operations, not for direct integration within application code.
incorrectExplanations.B: AWS CodeDeploy: Used for deploying applications to AWS environments, not for embedding service logic.
incorrectExplanations.D: AWS CodePipeline: Automates the software release process but doesn't embed AWS features into your code.

questions.question:
A startup company has deployed their application and databases on AWS. To reduce operational overhead, they want AWS to handle as many routine infrastructure tasks as possible, so their team can focus on innovation and business logic.
Which of the following tasks can AWS manage on their behalf? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Taking a backup of a database

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
a) Taking a backup of a database
b) Patching database software
questions.explanation:
a) Services like Amazon RDS and DynamoDB automate database backups, allowing users to enable scheduled backups and point-in-time recovery.
b) AWS manages software patching for managed services like RDS, relieving customers from manual maintenance tasks.

incorrectExplanations.C: AWS does not audit your source code — this is the responsibility of the customer or third-party tools.
incorrectExplanations.D: AWS provides tools to secure applications but does not perform security testing on customer applications.
incorrectExplanations.E: Designing and creating the database schema is an application-level decision handled by the customer.

questions.question:
A company is evaluating different AWS compute and database services for hosting their application. They want to understand where they are responsible for tasks like patching the underlying operating system (OS).
In which of the following services is the customer responsible for patching the operating system?
questions.explanation: With Amazon EC2, customers manage the virtual machine, which includes patching the operating system and maintaining software updates — this is part of the shared responsibility model.

incorrectExplanations.A: AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine — AWS handles all infrastructure and OS patching.
incorrectExplanations.B: Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database — AWS manages all underlying infrastructure.
incorrectExplanations.D: AWS Lambda runs code without provisioning servers — OS management is handled entirely by AWS.

questions.question:
A media company hosts all its video content in a single Amazon S3 bucket located in the US East (N. Virginia) region. As their global audience grows, users in distant regions are experiencing increased latency while streaming videos.
According to the performance pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework, which service should the company use to ensure low-latency access to the video content globally?

options.text: Use AWS CloudFront to cache the video content closer to end users.
Use Amazon ElastiCache to cache the video content closer to end users.
Use AWS DynamoDB DAX to cache the video content closer to end users.
Use Amazon Kinesis to cache the video content closer to end users.

questions.sourceAnswerKey: a) Use AWS CloudFront to cache the video content closer to end users.
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFront is a global Content Delivery Network (CDN) that caches content at edge locations near end users, which significantly reduces latency and improves video streaming performance for users worldwide.

incorrectExplanations.B: Amazon ElastiCache is used to cache database query results, not large video content.
incorrectExplanations.C: DynamoDB DAX is a caching layer for DynamoDB, not for static content like videos.
incorrectExplanations.D: Amazon Kinesis is for real-time data streaming and analytics, not content delivery or caching.

questions.question:
A database administrator is tasked with deploying and managing a highly available relational database for a production application. They are considering using Amazon RDS to reduce operational complexity and focus more on performance tuning and application logic.
Which of the following is a key advantage the administrator would gain by using Amazon RDS?

options.text: RDS enables users to dynamically adjust CPU and RAM resources.
RDS databases automatically scale based on load.
RDS simplifies relational database administration tasks.

questions.sourceAnswerKey: d) RDS simplifies relational database administration tasks.
questions.explanation: Amazon RDS is a fully managed service that automates tasks like backups, patching, monitoring, and failover, thereby reducing the administrative overhead for database admins.

incorrectExplanations.A: You must manually scale instance classes or use RDS Auto Scaling for read replicas; it's not dynamic like compute auto-scaling.
incorrectExplanations.B: RDS does not automatically scale compute resources based on load (except Aurora Serverless).
incorrectExplanations.C: 99.99999999999% refers to S3 durability, not RDS reliability or durability.

questions.question:
A financial services company is planning to use Amazon RDS to host its production databases. As part of their compliance audit, the team wants to know who is responsible for applying security patches to the RDS instances under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model.
Who is responsible for patching Amazon RDS database instances?
questions.explanation: In managed services like Amazon RDS, AWS is responsible for infrastructure-level patching and maintenance, including the underlying OS and database engine software.

questions.question:
An enterprise wants to migrate part of its on-premises file-based workloads to the cloud. The applications require standard NFS-based access and must be able to read/write objects to Amazon S3, with local caching to improve performance.
Which AWS service can best meet these requirements?

options.text: AWS Storage Gateway — Amazon S3 File Gateway

questions.sourceAnswerKey: c) AWS Storage Gateway — Amazon S3 File Gateway
questions.explanation: The Amazon S3 File Gateway allows on-premises applications to access Amazon S3 as if it were a file share using NFS or SMB protocols, with local caching capabilities.

questions.question:
An eCommerce platform uses an Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) to route traffic to a fleet of EC2 instances. One of the instances starts failing health checks.
What will ELB do in response to this unhealthy instance?

options.text: It only sends traffic to the remaining healthy instances.
It restarts the unhealthy EC2 instance.
It terminates the failed instance so that it is not part of the ELB target group.
It continues to send traffic to the failed instance.

questions.sourceAnswerKey: a) It only sends traffic to the remaining healthy instances
questions.explanation:
ELB stops routing traffic to any EC2 instance that fails health checks, ensuring that only healthy instances receive traffic. It does not take actions like restarting or terminating the instance.
Elastic Load Balancing Health Checks

questions.question:
A data analytics company is planning to archive a large volume of structured and unstructured data into Amazon S3. Their engineering lead wants to confirm the maximum storage limit per account.
How much data can be stored in Amazon S3?
questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 is designed to provide virtually unlimited object storage. Each object can be up to 5 TB, and there’s no limit to the total number of objects or amount of storage.
Amazon S3 Limits

questions.question:
A cloud architect is designing a secure web hosting environment on AWS. The solution must follow security best practices to minimize risk from external threats.
Where should firewalling and traffic filtering be implemented in the design?
questions.explanation:
Defense in depth is a key principle in AWS. Firewalls (like security groups and network ACLs) should be applied at multiple layers, including perimeter, network, and host level, to ensure layered security.
AWS Security Best Practices

questions.subtopic: Variable expenses and economies of scale
questions.question:
A startup is building a new analytics platform on AWS. Their workloads vary dramatically—low usage during the day and high spikes at night and weekends. The company wants a cost-efficient solution without committing to large upfront infrastructure costs.
Which TWO reasons explain why AWS is more economical than traditional data centers for applications with varying compute workloads?

options.text: Amazon EC2 costs are billed on a monthly basis.
Users retain full administrative access to their Amazon EC2 instances.
Amazon EC2 instances can be launched on demand when needed.
AWS allows automatic scaling of compute resources based on demand.

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
c) Amazon EC2 instances can be launched on demand when needed
d) AWS allows automatic scaling of compute resources based on demand
questions.explanation:
c) Amazon EC2 instances can be launched on demand when needed:
This allows you to avoid paying for idle resources. You pay only when an instance is running, making it ideal for workloads with unpredictable spikes.
d) AWS allows automatic scaling of compute resources based on demand:
Services like Auto Scaling and Elastic Load Balancing allow resources to grow and shrink dynamically, helping you avoid over-provisioning and reduce costs.

incorrectExplanations.A:
Amazon EC2 costs are billed on a monthly basis:
Not true — EC2 charges per second (Linux) or per hour (Windows), not monthly. Monthly billing is a characteristic of traditional hosting, not AWS.
incorrectExplanations.B:
Users retain full administrative access to their Amazon EC2 instances:
While technically true, this is related to control and configuration, not cost efficiency.

questions.question:
An organization recently migrated its applications to AWS. The security team wants to ensure that the infrastructure follows best practices, such as restricted security groups, unused access keys, and proper IAM permissions. They are looking for a tool that can provide real-time recommendations for improving infrastructure security and cost optimization.
Which AWS service should they use to get these recommendations?

options.text: AWS Price List Application Programming Interface (API)
Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) Spot Fleet

questions.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor is a web-based tool that provides real-time recommendations for improving security, fault tolerance, performance, service limits, and cost optimization. It checks things like open ports, multi-factor authentication, and IAM usage — making it ideal for infrastructure security optimization.

incorrectExplanations.A:
AWS Price List API:
Used for retrieving pricing information — not related to security recommendations.
incorrectExplanations.B:
Reserved Instances:
Offer cost savings for predictable workloads but have no role in security optimization.
incorrectExplanations.D:
Amazon EC2 Spot Fleet:
Helps you manage and request Spot Instances for cost efficiency — not for security assessments or advice.

questions.question:
A system administrator is responsible for ensuring the health and performance of applications running on AWS. They need a solution that can collect and track operational metrics, such as CPU utilization, disk I/O, and custom application-level metrics, across various AWS services.
Which AWS service should the administrator use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch is the AWS-native monitoring service that collects and tracks metrics, logs, and events from AWS resources and applications. It enables real-time monitoring and alarming to detect anomalies and operational issues.

incorrectExplanations.A:
Amazon CloudFront:
A Content Delivery Network (CDN) used to deliver content with low latency. It’s not used for collecting metrics across AWS services.
incorrectExplanations.B:
Amazon CloudSearch:
A search service for integrating search functionality into applications — not for performance monitoring or metrics collection.
incorrectExplanations.D:
Amazon Machine Learning (Amazon ML):
Used for creating and training machine learning models — unrelated to infrastructure monitoring or metrics tracking.

questions.question:
An operations engineer is tasked with monitoring AWS infrastructure for a rapidly growing SaaS platform. The engineer needs a solution to collect metrics, track resource utilization, set alarms, and automate responses when thresholds are breached (e.g., CPU usage over 80% for EC2 instances).
Which AWS service provides these monitoring and automation capabilities?
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch is the AWS service that collects and tracks metrics, logs, and events from AWS services and custom applications. It allows users to set alarms, visualize performance metrics, and automate actions based on thresholds (like scaling or notifications).

incorrectExplanations.A:
Amazon CloudFront:
A Content Delivery Network (CDN) used for low-latency delivery of content — it does not track metrics.
incorrectExplanations.B:
Amazon CloudSearch:
A managed search service to index and search text — unrelated to system monitoring or metrics.
incorrectExplanations.D:
Amazon Machine Learning (Amazon ML):
Used for building and deploying machine learning models — not for monitoring or metric tracking.

questions.question:
An IT administrator is setting up a new web application for their company on AWS. As part of the setup, they need to register a custom domain name (e.g., example.com) to use for accessing the application. The administrator prefers to manage DNS settings and domain registration within AWS itself.
Which AWS service should the administrator use to register the domain name?
questions.explanation: Amazon Route 53 is AWS's scalable Domain Name System (DNS) web service that also supports domain name registration. It allows administrators to register new domains, manage DNS records, and route end users to applications hosted on AWS or elsewhere.

incorrectExplanations.B:
Amazon CloudFront:
A Content Delivery Network (CDN) used for low-latency content delivery — not for registering domain names.
incorrectExplanations.C:
Elastic Load Balancing:
Distributes traffic across multiple targets like EC2 instances — it has no role in domain registration.
incorrectExplanations.D:
Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC):
Let's you provision logically isolated cloud networks — unrelated to domain name registration or DNS.

questions.question:
A DevOps engineer at a fast-growing startup is tasked with automating the deployment and scaling of cloud infrastructure. The team wants to avoid manual configuration through the AWS Management Console and instead integrate infrastructure provisioning directly into their CI/CD pipeline using scripts and tools like Terraform or AWS CLI.
What is the key benefit of having AWS services accessible through an Application Programming Interface (API)?

options.text: Cloud resources can be managed programmatically
AWS infrastructure use will always be cost-optimized
All application testing is managed by AWS

questions.sourceAnswerKey: a) Cloud resources can be managed programmatically
questions.explanation: Using AWS APIs allows developers and system administrators to automate tasks such as creating, managing, and terminating resources through scripts or third-party tools. This improves efficiency, repeatability, and supports infrastructure as code (IaC) practices.

incorrectExplanations.B:
AWS infrastructure use will always be cost-optimized:
Cost optimization is achieved through monitoring and right-sizing, not simply by using APIs.
incorrectExplanations.C:
All application testing is managed by AWS:
Application testing remains the customer’s responsibility. AWS provides tools but does not automatically manage testing.
incorrectExplanations.D:
Customer-owned, on-premises infrastructure becomes programmable:
AWS APIs manage cloud resources, not on-premises infrastructure, unless additional integration (like AWS Outposts) is in place

questions.question:
A cloud architect is tasked with designing a high-availability web application that must remain operational even if parts of the infrastructure experience failure. The architect is following the AWS Well-Architected Framework, particularly the principle of "Design for failure and nothing will fail."
Which of the following actions best aligns with this design principle?

options.text: Adding an Elastic Load Balancer in front of a single Amazon EC2 instance
Creating and deploying the most cost-effective solution
Deploying the application in multiple Availability Zones
Using Amazon CloudWatch alerts to monitor performance

questions.sourceAnswerKey: c) Deploying the application in multiple Availability Zones
questions.explanation: Deploying across multiple Availability Zones (AZs) ensures that if one AZ fails, the application remains available in others. This is a core strategy for fault tolerance and aligns directly with the "design for failure" principle

incorrectExplanations.A:
Adding an Elastic Load Balancer in front of a single Amazon EC2 instance
This doesn't eliminate single points of failure. The EC2 instance is still a bottleneck.
incorrectExplanations.B:
Creating and deploying the most cost-effective solution
While cost optimization is important, it is not related to fault tolerance or failure design.
incorrectExplanations.D:
Using Amazon CloudWatch alerts to monitor performance
Monitoring helps with detection, not prevention of failure. It’s reactive, not proactive design.

questions.question:
A new system administrator at a company is tasked with setting up user access for different teams in their AWS account. The administrator needs to create individual users, assign specific permissions to them (e.g., read-only access to S3, full access to EC2), and ensure that only authorized individuals can access specific AWS services.
Which AWS service should the administrator use to manage these user permissions and roles?
questions.sourceAnswerKey: d) AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
questions.explanation: AWS IAM enables administrators to securely control access to AWS services and resources. It lets you create users, groups, and roles, and assign permissions via policies. IAM is the central service for managing authentication and authorization in AWS.

incorrectExplanations.A:
AWS Config
Used to track configuration changes and compliance—not to assign permissions.
incorrectExplanations.B:
AWS CloudTrail
Used to log and monitor API activity, not to manage user access.
incorrectExplanations.C:
AWS KMS
Used to create and control encryption keys, not user or permission management.

questions.question:
A data engineer is building a centralized data warehouse solution to handle large-scale analytics workloads for a retail company. The solution must be able to automatically provision infrastructure, perform administrative tasks such as backups and patching, and scale to accommodate complex analytical queries on structured data.
Which AWS service is the most appropriate for this use case?
questions.explanation: Amazon Redshift is a fully managed, petabyte-scale data warehouse service designed specifically for analytical workloads. It automates infrastructure provisioning, patching, backups, and scaling, allowing teams to focus on data analysis instead of operations.

incorrectExplanations.B:
Amazon DynamoDB
A NoSQL key-value and document database service—not designed for complex analytical workloads.
incorrectExplanations.C:
Amazon ElastiCache
Primarily used to cache frequently accessed data to improve application performance—not for data warehousing.
incorrectExplanations.D:
Amazon Aurora
A relational database service suitable for transactional (OLTP) workloads—not optimized for large-scale analytical queries.

questions.question:
A cloud engineer is reviewing their company’s responsibilities under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model. They are specifically tasked with controlling user access to resources within their AWS environment and want to ensure that they are properly following best practices for securing the application stack.
According to the Shared Responsibility Model, which of the following is the customer responsible for?

options.text: Managing AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)

questions.sourceAnswerKey: a) Managing AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
questions.explanation: In the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, customers are responsible for security in the cloud, which includes managing IAM roles and policies, configuring security groups, patching applications, and encrypting data. IAM helps control who can access what within your AWS environment.

incorrectExplanations.B:
Securing edge locations
AWS is responsible for securing its global infrastructure, including edge locations.
incorrectExplanations.C:
Monitoring physical device security
Physical hardware and data center security fall under AWS’s responsibility.
incorrectExplanations.D:
Implementing Service Organization Control (SOC) standards
AWS obtains and manages SOC certifications for its infrastructure; customers may use them as part of their compliance reporting but are not responsible for implementation.

questions.question:
A finance analyst at a company is investigating an unexpected spike in compute costs from three months ago. The analyst needs to review historical billing activity specifically related to Amazon EC2 usage in order to understand what caused the increase.
Which AWS service should the analyst use to access detailed historical billing and usage data?

options.text: AWS CloudTrail logs stored in Amazon S3

questions.sourceAnswerKey: b) AWS Cost and Usage Reports
questions.explanation: The AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR) provide detailed billing information, including usage by service, region, tags, and accounts. It’s the most granular source for historical billing analysis and is ideal for reviewing EC2 activity from three months ago or earlier.

incorrectExplanations.A:
Amazon EC2 dashboard
Shows current EC2 instance statuses and settings but does not include detailed billing history.
incorrectExplanations.C:
AWS Trusted Advisor dashboard
Provides real-time recommendations for cost optimization, security, and performance, but not historical billing data.
incorrectExplanations.D:
AWS CloudTrail logs stored in Amazon S3
Tracks API activity, not cost or billing data. It’s useful for security audits, not cost analysis.

questions.question:
A company is undergoing a cloud security audit and the auditor asks, "Who ultimately has ownership and control of the data stored in your AWS account, including decisions about data access, encryption, and deletion?"
The cloud administrator must identify which parties have direct control over the data stored and processed in their AWS environment.
Which TWO entities have control of the data in an AWS account?
(Choose TWO)
questions.sourceAnswerKey:
b) AWS Account Owner
e) IAM Users with delegated permissions
questions.explanation:
b) AWS Account Owner: The account owner has full administrative control over all AWS resources and data. They define access policies, manage billing, and determine who can interact with data.
e) IAM Users with delegated permissions: IAM users or roles granted access by the account owner can manage, modify, or delete data, depending on their permissions.

incorrectExplanations.A:
AWS Support Team
AWS Support can assist with infrastructure issues but does not access or control customer data unless explicitly granted permission for troubleshooting.
incorrectExplanations.C:
AWS Security Team
AWS is responsible for securing the infrastructure, not managing customer data.
incorrectExplanations.D:
AWS Technical Account Manager (TAM)
TAMs provide advisory support, but they do not have access or control over customer data.

questions.question:
A solutions architect is tasked with improving the reliability and scalability of a monolithic application. To achieve this, they decide to break the application into independent components that can communicate through asynchronous messaging using services like Amazon SQS or SNS.
What are the primary benefits of decoupling an application into smaller, loosely connected components?
(Choose TWO)

options.text: Reduce inter-dependencies so failures do not impact other components
Enable data synchronization across the web application layer
Have the ability to execute automated bootstrapping actions
Increase fault tolerance and flexibility in scaling

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
b) Reduce inter-dependencies so failures do not impact other components
e) Increase fault tolerance and flexibility in scaling
questions.explanation:
b) Decoupling helps prevent cascading failures—if one component fails, others can continue functioning.
e) Decoupled systems allow components to scale independently, enhancing fault tolerance and resource optimization.

incorrectExplanations.A: Tightly integrated applications are the opposite of decoupled; they increase failure impact and reduce flexibility.
incorrectExplanations.C: Data synchronization is not the goal of decoupling. The focus is on reducing direct dependencies.
incorrectExplanations.D: Automated bootstrapping (e.g., using EC2 user data scripts) is a deployment feature, not a benefit of decoupling the architecture.

questions.question:
A company is designing a mission-critical application that must remain highly available even during failures in part of the infrastructure. The solutions architect recommends deploying the application across two Availability Zones (AZs) to meet this requirement.
What is the key benefit of deploying the application across multiple Availability Zones?

options.text: Performance is improved over running in a single Availability Zone
It is more secure than running in a single Availability Zone
It significantly reduces the total cost of ownership versus running in a single Availability Zone
It increases the availability of an application compared to running in a single Availability Zone

questions.sourceAnswerKey: d) It increases the availability of an application compared to running in a single Availability Zone
questions.explanation: Running your application across multiple Availability Zones provides redundancy and fault tolerance. If one AZ goes down, the other can continue serving traffic, which improves overall application availability.

incorrectExplanations.A: Performance gains are not guaranteed just by spanning AZs; latency may even slightly increase due to cross-AZ communication.
incorrectExplanations.B: Security posture is not automatically improved by spreading across AZs. Security depends on IAM, encryption, and security group settings.
incorrectExplanations.C: Costs may increase, not decrease, since you're running resources in more than one zone.

questions.question:
A security engineer is reviewing their organization's responsibilities under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model. The engineer must ensure that security settings under the customer’s control are properly configured while AWS manages the underlying infrastructure.
Which TWO responsibilities fall under the control of the AWS customer?
(Choose TWO)
questions.sourceAnswerKey:
a) Password policies
b) User permissions
questions.explanation:
a) Password policies: Customers define and enforce IAM password policies such as complexity rules and rotation periods.
b) User permissions: Customers are responsible for managing IAM users, groups, and the policies that govern their access to AWS resources.

incorrectExplanations.C: Physical security: This is AWS’s responsibility—they manage physical data center access and security.
incorrectExplanations.D: Disk disposal: AWS handles the secure decommissioning and physical destruction of storage media.
incorrectExplanations.E: Hardware patching: AWS is responsible for maintaining and patching the underlying hardware infrastructure.

questions.question:
A startup is launching a new e-commerce platform on AWS and expects fluctuating traffic, especially during seasonal sales. The cloud architect recommends applying the cloud architecture principle of elasticity to ensure optimal performance and cost-efficiency during these traffic spikes.
How does designing for elasticity benefit the application in this scenario?

options.text: Minimize storage requirements by reducing logging and auditing activities
Create systems that scale to the required capacity based on changes in demand
Enable AWS to automatically select the most cost-effective services
Accelerate the design process because recovery from failure is automated, reducing the need for testing

questions.sourceAnswerKey: b) Create systems that scale to the required capacity based on changes in demand
questions.explanation: Elastic systems can automatically scale up or down in response to demand, which is ideal for unpredictable or bursty workloads like online retail. This optimizes both performance and cost.

incorrectExplanations.A: Logging and auditing are unrelated to elasticity; reducing them may compromise compliance or troubleshooting.
incorrectExplanations.C: AWS offers cost tools, but elasticity is about scaling, not selecting services.
incorrectExplanations.D: Elasticity and automated recovery improve reliability, but don't eliminate the need for testing or significantly accelerate the design process.

questions.question:
A data analytics company is looking to reduce its compute costs on AWS. They have several batch processing and data transformation jobs that run multiple times a day but do not require guaranteed uptime. A cloud engineer recommends using Amazon EC2 Spot Instances to handle these workloads.
Which TWO characteristics make Spot Instances appropriate for this scenario?
(Choose TWO)

options.text: Workloads that are only run in the morning and stopped at night
Workloads where the availability of the Amazon EC2 instances can be flexible
Workloads that need to run for long periods of time without interruption
Workloads that are critical and need Amazon EC2 instances with termination protection
Workloads that can tolerate interruptions and be restarted from checkpoints

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
b) Workloads where the availability of the Amazon EC2 instances can be flexible
e) Workloads that can tolerate interruptions and be restarted from checkpoints
questions.explanation:
b) Spot instances are ideal when you can be flexible about when your workloads run, as they may be interrupted when capacity is no longer available.
e) They are most effective for interruptible workloads that can resume from a saved state or checkpoint (like data analysis or rendering).

incorrectExplanations.A: This describes a predictable schedule, better suited for Scheduled Reserved Instances or Savings Plans, not Spot Instances.
incorrectExplanations.C: Long-running, non-interruptible workloads are not ideal for Spot, as they could be terminated mid-process.
incorrectExplanations.D: Spot instances can be terminated at any time by AWS and do not support termination protection, making them unsuitable for critical applications.

questions.question:
A new DevOps engineer joins your team and needs to interact with AWS services for provisioning resources, managing configurations, and monitoring infrastructure. The engineer wants to use a web-based interface for visibility and control but also wants to automate some tasks via code.
Which TWO AWS features will allow the engineer to manage AWS services in these ways?
(Choose TWO)
questions.sourceAnswerKey:
a) AWS Management Console
b) AWS Application Programming Interface (API)
questions.explanation:
a) AWS Management Console is a web-based user interface that enables users to visually interact with AWS services, launch resources, view logs, configure security settings, and more.
b) AWS APIs provide programmatic access to AWS services and are commonly used in automation tools and script.

incorrectExplanations.C: AWS SDKs are programming libraries for various languages (like Python, Java, etc.) and are built on top of AWS APIs. SDKs help simplify API calls, but they are not a web-based UI.
incorrectExplanations.D: Amazon CloudWatch is a monitoring and observability service, not a management interface. It’s used for logging, metrics, and alerting, not for provisioning or managing AWS services.

questions.question:
A cloud financial analyst at a company is tasked with reviewing the distribution of AWS costs across departments and services. They need a tool that provides visualizations, filtering by account or service, and cost trends over time to help with budget forecasting and chargebacks.
Which TWO AWS tools can assist in analyzing and displaying AWS spending distribution?
(Choose TWO)
questions.sourceAnswerKey:
a) AWS Organizations
d) AWS Cost Explorer
questions.explanation:
a) AWS Organizations – Allows consolidated billing and cost allocation across multiple linked accounts. It lets you group and track spend by organizational unit or account.
d) AWS Cost Explorer – Provides interactive dashboards to view and analyze costs by service, linked account, usage type, and more. Ideal for visualizing spending trends and forecasting future costs.

incorrectExplanations.B: Amazon DevPay – An outdated tool used for billing third-party developers. It’s not used to analyze your AWS spending.
incorrectExplanations.C: AWS Trusted Advisor – Focuses on best practices related to security, performance, fault tolerance, and cost optimization recommendations, not cost distribution visualization.

technicalReview.reason: Check whether Organizations meets the stated analysis and visualization requirement alongside Cost Explorer.

questions.question:
A cloud administrator is tasked with strengthening the security of the AWS Management Console for all users in an organization. The goal is to prevent unauthorized access and enhance account protection, especially for accounts with elevated privileges.
Which TWO measures should the administrator implement to secure access to the AWS Management Console?
(Choose TWO)

options.text: Disable AWS console access for users who don’t need it

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
a) Apply Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
d) Disable AWS console access for users who don’t need it
questions.explanation:
a) MFA adds an extra layer of security by requiring a second factor (like an OTP from an authenticator app), making unauthorized access significantly harder.
d) Disabling AWS console access for users who don’t need it follows the principle of least privilege, reducing the attack surface by limiting access only to those who require it.

incorrectExplanations.B: AWS does not support a “secondary password” feature. MFA is the recommended secure practice instead.
incorrectExplanations.C: Root access should be used sparingly and never requested unless necessary. Encouraging more root access increases security risks.

questions.question:
A security engineer is tasked with improving the account protection measures across an organization’s AWS environment. As part of the security enhancement, the engineer must enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for all AWS users to ensure that access to the environment is properly secured.
Which TWO AWS services can the engineer use to enable and manage MFA?
(Choose TWO)
questions.sourceAnswerKey:
a) AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
d) AWS Management Console
questions.explanation:
a) AWS IAM is the core service used to configure and enforce MFA. IAM lets you enable MFA for users and roles, manage devices, and require MFA for privileged actions.
d) AWS Management Console provides the user interface where users can register MFA devices and configure MFA settings under their IAM security credentials.

incorrectExplanations.B: Amazon EC2 is used for virtual servers and has no role in configuring or enforcing MFA for user accounts.
incorrectExplanations.C: AWS Config tracks resource configuration changes and compliance but does not configure security credentials or MFA

questions.question:
A company is building a disaster recovery (DR) plan to ensure business continuity in case of a major infrastructure failure. The cloud architect is asked to design the strategy using AWS services so that critical workloads can be recovered and run independently from the affected environment in the event of a disaster.
Which TWO AWS infrastructure components should the company consider using to launch disaster recovery resources in a separate location?
(Choose TWO)
questions.sourceAnswerKey:
b) AWS Region
d) Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC)
questions.explanation:
b) AWS Region: A DR strategy typically requires launching backup infrastructure in a different Region to protect against regional failures (e.g., natural disasters).
d) Amazon VPC: For isolation and control, disaster recovery environments are usually created in a separate VPC within the DR Region, allowing for network-level configuration and security.

incorrectExplanations.A: Subnet: Subnets are subdivisions within a VPC and do not provide geographic separation. They cannot serve as independent DR environments.
incorrectExplanations.C: AWS edge location: These are used for content delivery via CloudFront and not intended for hosting full infrastructure or DR environments.

questions.question:
A company is preparing to migrate their infrastructure to the AWS Cloud. The cloud architect has been asked to estimate the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) to evaluate the financial benefits of the move. As part of this process, the architect must consider all relevant factors that will impact cost savings and ROI.
Which TWO factors should the architect consider when calculating the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) for the AWS Cloud?
(Choose TWO)

options.text: The number of servers migrated to AWS
The number of users migrated to AWS
The number of passwords migrated to AWS
The number of keys migrated to AWS

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
a) The number of servers migrated to AWS
b) The number of users migrated to AWS
questions.explanation:
a) Number of servers migrated to AWS: The count of physical or virtual servers directly affects compute, storage, and licensing costs—a critical TCO component.
b) Number of users migrated to AWS: This impacts the type and volume of services needed, including IAM permissions, support plans, and user-level configurations (e.g., Workspaces, SSO).

incorrectExplanations.C: Number of passwords migrated to AWS: Passwords themselves do not contribute to cost. They are related to security practices, not TCO.
incorrectExplanations.D: Number of keys migrated to AWS: While important for security, migrating cryptographic keys has minimal to no impact on cost estimation in TCO models.

questions.question:
A media company is expanding globally and needs to deliver high-quality video content to users in multiple countries with low latency and high transfer speeds. To optimize performance and reduce load on the origin servers, the company wants to implement a global content delivery strategy using AWS services.
Which TWO AWS services can help achieve this goal by acting as or supporting a Content Delivery Network (CDN)?
(Choose TWO)
questions.sourceAnswerKey:
c) Amazon CloudFront
d) Amazon S3
questions.explanation:
c) Amazon CloudFront is AWS’s global CDN service. It caches content at edge locations to deliver it with low latency and high transfer speeds to users worldwide.
d) Amazon S3 stores the original static content (like images, videos, HTML) that CloudFront can cache and serve through its edge locations globally.

incorrectExplanations.A: Amazon SES (Simple Email Service) is used for email delivery, not for content distribution or CDN functionality.
incorrectExplanations.B: Amazon CloudTrail records API calls for auditing and compliance. It does not serve or distribute content to end users.

questions.question:
A company performs annual compliance audits and wants to store large volumes of rarely accessed historical data, such as logs and reports. They are looking for a cost-effective storage solution that provides long-term durability but does not require frequent access.
Which TWO AWS services should the company consider for this use case?
(Choose TWO)

options.text: Amazon S3 Glacier (now part of Amazon S3 Archive classes)
Amazon S3 (Standard or Infrequent Access classes)

questions.sourceAnswerKey:
b) Amazon S3 Glacier
d) Amazon S3
questions.explanation:
b) Amazon S3 Glacier is ideal for long-term, infrequent access and archival storage. It offers low-cost storage with retrieval times ranging from minutes to hours.
d) Amazon S3 offers different storage classes, including S3 Standard-Infrequent Access and S3 Intelligent-Tiering, which are suitable for cost-efficient storage of data that is not accessed often

incorrectExplanations.A: Amazon Storage Gateway is a hybrid cloud storage service for integrating on-premises environments with AWS. It is not the most cost-effective choice for archive-only data.
incorrectExplanations.C: Amazon EBS (Elastic Block Store) is designed for block storage with high IOPS and low latency. It is more expensive and suited for active, frequently accessed data, not archival.

questions.question:
A startup is building a scalable e-commerce platform that requires a fully managed NoSQL database capable of handling millions of read/write requests per second with low latency and high availability. The development team wants to avoid managing infrastructure, scaling, or software patching.
Which TWO database services should they consider using on AWS?
(Choose TWO)
questions.sourceAnswerKey:
b) AWS DynamoDB
d) AWS MongoDB (self-hosted)
questions.explanation:
b) AWS DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database provided by AWS. It supports key-value and document-based models, offers single-digit millisecond latency, automatic scaling, and serverless operation.
d) AWS MongoDB is not natively provided by AWS as a managed service, but you can run MongoDB on EC2 or use Amazon DocumentDB, which is MongoDB-compatible and fully managed. So technically, MongoDB on AWS (self-managed or via DocumentDB) can be considered, although it's not a native AWS-managed service like DynamoDB.

incorrectExplanations.A: AWS RDS is a managed relational database service, not a NoSQL solution.
incorrectExplanations.C: AWS Redshift is a data warehousing service used for OLAP (Online Analytical Processing), not for NoSQL use cases or high-throughput transactional workloads.

questions.question:
